#5154. CZ Urges 1Password Users to Change All Their Passwords

After a hacker stole customer data, Binance founder Changpeng Zhao advised 1Password users to change all the passwords stored in the service.

1Password offered different advice about what users should do after the incident was disclosed on Nov. 25. The password management service said hackers hadn't gained access to the passwords stored in users' vaults, so there was no need to reset them.

"If you use 1Password, recommend you to change ALL your passwords. It's a pain in the neck, but necessary," Zhao said on X, replying to a post from Coin Bureau about the breach.

If you have a crypto exchange login stored in 1Password, this distinction is important.

1Password says hackers could access the email address a customer uses to log in to the service. But they couldn't see the exchange password saved in the customer's vault.

Scammers could still use the stolen email addresses to contact people they know are 1Password users.

1Password started investigating on Nov. 19 after detecting signs of possible unauthorized access to an employee's corporate GitHub account.

From there, the hacker was able to steal private source code and inject malicious code into 1Password's backend services. The malicious code then downloaded certain administrative data about customers.

1Password publicly disclosed the breach on Nov. 25, six days later.

The company did not specify how many customers were affected or explain exactly how the hacker managed to take over the employee's account.

The stolen data included customer names, login email addresses, account and user IDs, and timestamps indicating account creation and last use.

The hacker also gained access to 1Password's software development and deployment systems.

1Password disabled the compromised employee's GitHub account and revoked the stolen access token.

The company also restored a clean version of the affected service and revoked or replaced potentially exposed internal credentials.

1Password also engaged independent security experts to review its response.

1Password recommends that customers check the 1Password app or type the company's website address directly into their browser if they receive an unexpected invitation or recovery message.

The company says it will never contact users to request their account password or Secret Key.

Update: 1Password claims that there is no need to change one's 1Password account password or any of the passwords saved in one's vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident.

Hi CZ! There’s no need to change your 1Password account password or any of the passwords you’ve saved in your vault. No customer passwords were exposed in this incident. We don’t store your account password or Secret Key, and getting into our backend systems didn’t give the attacker the keys to decrypt your vault. The attacker did copy account information for some customers, including names and email addresses, so we recommend watching for 1Password invitations or account recovery emails you weren’t expecting. You can read the full update on our blog: https://t.co/9fbzzAJr0B

#5153. Jade Cargill Was a Basketball Player Before the WWE. Here’s What Changed Everything

The 34-year-old wrestling superstar stops byThe Huddle ahead of her appearance on Survivor Series: WarGames on November 28th.

Given the ease with which WWE superstar Jade Cargill delivers a pump kick or spinebuster, it’s hard to believe the 34-year-old hasn’t spent her entire life in the ring. But growing up, Jade was obsessed with a different sport: basketball. In college, she was a forward/guard for the Jacksonville University team then went on to play overseas in France.

The experience of being a team player has come in handy for Jade as she navigates the world of wrestling. Sure, it may often look like a one-on-one competition, but Jade says that, if anything, it’s more like a dance.

“I can only be as great as my partner,” she tells editors Abigail Cuffey, Amanda Lucci, and Jacqueline Andriakos on the latest episode of The Huddle. “I can't do this by myself.”

Despite having been a part of the WWE since 2023, Jade admits she’s still a “rookie” compared to her ‘dance’ partners—the other women in the league, who inspire her every day. “I've been placed in a very amazing environment with women who strive for greatness, and that's what I want to do,” she says.

As she prepares to lead a five-woman team at Survivor Series: WarGames on November 28, Jade talks about her unconventional path to wrestling, making peace with mistakes, and the advice she wants every kid watching her to hear.

Jade’s journey to becoming a professional wrestler is the stuff of motivational sports movies. A stay-at-home mom (she took time off work as a child psychologist to raise her daughter), Jade was simply training in the gym to get strong after pregnancy when she was introduced to WWE veteran Mark Henry, who asked if she’d ever considered a career in wrestling.

“I was like, ‘Why not?’” she recalls thinking. “I had a kid and put my life on hold for a little bit. I wanted to do something more. I was like, ‘This body is not done.’ [I] went to a tryout, had no experience at all.”

Jade left that tryout bruised and battered—and determined to improve. And so she trained and trained and trained some more. She couldn’t get enough. “I just loved it,” she says. “It's athletics, yes, but also it's improvising, but also it's acting, but also it's your natural instinct. It’s all these things wrapped into one that I just didn't want to put down.”

All that work eventually paid off: Jade made her professional wrestling debut with All Elite Wrestling in 2020 and then joined the WWE three years later.

Despite all the training and preparation that goes into a match, Jade admits that not a single one has been “perfect.” But in the case where she stumbles off the ropes or throws a lousy punch, Jade simply follows the old maxim, the show must go on.

“I just kind of have the mindset that these things happen,” she says. “If you do have a mishap, you can't sell it—[the audience doesn’t] know what's going on. You just got to keep going with the punches.”

Jade also gives a lot of credit to her fellow competitors, who often pick her up—if not physically, then emotionally—after a match, letting her know she’s not alone.

“I remember my coworker Naomi sent me a clip of her falling, and she was like, ‘Just to show you...’ And I was like, ‘Okay, all right. It happens,’” Jade says. “You’ve just got to keep on going and make your next match the best match.”

As a mom, Jade knows how powerful an adult’s example can be—whether it’s a parent’s or a performer’s. Ultimately, she hopes kids are inspired by her hard work and determination, both in and out of the ring, and if they can take away any message, it would be this: “Don't let anyone tell you who you are,” she says. “Don't let society put you in a box. Go out there and take on the world.”

And when a new opportunity presents itself, don’t be afraid to give it a try. “If you would have told me five years ago, I would be wrestling. I would have laughed,” she says. “And look at me now.”

To hear more from Jade—including her no-frills recovery program—click play on the latest episode of The Huddle above.

Available in Standard and Platinum editions, the BASIS Card offers up to 10% cashback, with applicants selecting their preferred tier subject to staking eligibility

The BASIS Card returns money differently. Announced today by BASIS DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE LTD, the payment card credits cashback in the asset used for each eligible purchase, with Platinum cardholders qualifying for 10% cashback during the introductory Launch Boost period.

For digital asset holders, the principle is straightforward. Spend Bitcoin and receive Bitcoin back. Pay with Ethereum and receive Ethereum back. There are no reward points to redeem or proprietary platform tokens to manage. Cashback is credited in an asset the cardholder already uses, giving everyday spending a direct connection to their digital asset holdings.

Opening first-round applications expands BASIS’s existing digital asset infrastructure into everyday payments. Applications are submitted at https://basis.pro/card and close on December 31, 2026, at 23:59 UTC.

The BASIS Card is available in Standard, finished in matte black composite, and Platinum, produced in metal. Applicants select their preferred edition when submitting their waitlist application, with qualification determined by their active staking position.

Each edition has a separate staking eligibility threshold, as detailed below. BASIS measures the value of the applicant’s active staking position against the requirement for their selected tier. The position is assessed at submission and re-checked at the close of the application period.

Participants can therefore review the benefits of each edition alongside its staking requirements before deciding which card to apply for. Final issuance remains subject to the issuing partner’s independent review.

Both editions feature an introductory Launch Boost period that begins on the date of card issuance. During this period, cardholders receive enhanced cashback rates, higher monthly reward caps, and additional subscription benefits.

*All monetary figures are expressed in USD. Physical card issuance fees include applicable shipping charges.

Launch Boost runs for three months following issuance, after which each card returns to its respective base benefits. Standard and Platinum also feature rate-lock periods of 12 and 24 months, respectively, subject to the applicable program terms.

Along with cashback, the card program brings together subscription rebates of 50% or 100%, depending on the edition and benefit period, across a catalog of over 80 subscriptions. Travel and additional card benefits include two annual airport lounge visits, a 3 GB eSIM, and one additional card, subject to tier eligibility and applicable terms. Standard cardholders benefit from a 2% FX fee, while Platinum cardholders pay no FX fee during Launch Boost. Both editions provide immediate access to a virtual card upon activation, with Platinum participants also receiving priority and dedicated support.

The defining feature of the BASIS Card is what happens after a purchase. Where conventional reward programs may require cardholders to accumulate points or convert rewards into their preferred currency, BASIS keeps the cashback denomination consistent with the asset spent.

Cashback on eligible settled purchases is credited directly to the cardholder’s Funding Wallet. A purchase made using BTC returns BTC, leaving the recipient free to decide how to use the reward.

Cardholders who wish to stake their cashback can do so separately under the platform’s ordinary conversion rules. Cashback does not automatically enter an existing staking position, and card rewards remain independent of staking yield.

Submitting a card application also leaves existing staking positions, lock-up periods, Dynamic Reward Rates, boosters, and stToken balances unchanged.

Applications are free and limited to one per account during Round 01. Participants must hold at least USD 1,000 in eligible BASIS wallet value at submission, maintain an account in good standing, and satisfy the staking requirements for their selected card edition.

Once BASIS approves a waitlist application, the applicant receives further instructions and a secure Know Your Customer (KYC) verification link. The issuing partner then conducts its own review, covering identity verification, residency, regional eligibility, sanctions screening, and supporting documentation.

Waitlist approval permits applicants to proceed to the next stage and does not constitute final card approval, activation, or issuance.

The rebound barely dents a brutal month. Bitcoin is still down 20% in November, from $77,580 on November 1. So is this a Thanksgiving pump, and does Bitcoin have a holiday-season pattern? We checked every Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year since 2013.

The answer is mostly no. Bitcoin rose over Thanksgiving weekend in only 6 of 13 years, and over Christmas in 5 of 13.

Is there no correlation at all? New Year is the exception: Bitcoin gained between December 30 and January 2 in 12 of the last 13 years.

All three assets rebounded after a rough Wednesday, when hot inflation data sealed a December Fed rate hike. Bitcoin rose 8% from its $57,300 low to $61,780, its highest level since Monday.

The metals moved faster. US gold futures climbed 4.6% from Wednesday’s close to $3,699 an ounce. Silver did even better, jumping 11.4% to $44.60. Analysts tied the rebound to a weaker US dollar.

The timing matters. US markets were closed on Thursday and trade only half a day on Friday, so thin volume made every move look bigger.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

To put Bitcoin news today in context, we measured bitcoin’s price change in three holiday windows every year from 2013 to 2025, using Bitstamp’s daily closing prices.

Thanksgiving weekend, from Wednesday’s close to Sunday’s, has been a coin flip. Bitcoin rose in 6 of 13 years, and the median move was -0.1%. The swings were large in both directions, from a 13.2% drop in 2018 to 12.9% gains in 2015 and 2017.

Christmas was no better. Between December 23 and 26, bitcoin rose in only 5 of 13 years, again with a median move of -0.1%.

New Year stands out. From December 30 to January 2, bitcoin gained in 12 of the last 13 years, with a median rise of 1.8%. The only drop came in 2019. The gain is small, but it keeps repeating, perhaps because some funds and traders put fresh cash to work at the start of the year.

EXPLORE: BTC News Today: US Bitcoin Strategic Reserve Bill Moves Closer as BTC Reclaims $60K

From the day before Thanksgiving to January 2, Bitcoin rose in 7 of 13 years, and the size of the move tracked its four-year cycle. In bull years the season was spectacular: bitcoin gained 79% in 2017 and 72% in 2020. In the years after a cycle top, it disappointed, with 14% drops in both 2014 and 2018 and a flat season in 2022.

The gains also tended to fade once the holidays ended. Bitcoin fell in January in 8 of 13 years, with a median drop of 5.4%.

This year looks more like the post-top years. Bitcoin peaked in October 2025 and is down more than half since. So for Bitcoin news today, the lesson is that a holiday bounce has not yet changed the trend.

BTC trades at $61,780, below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $71,180, and its 200-day EMA at $74,450.

The takeaway from Bitcoin news today: history says the Thanksgiving bounce is a coin flip, and the season as a whole follows the cycle. If the pattern holds, the one date worth watching is the turn of the year.

#5150. XRP ETF Buyers Suddenly Return

U.S. spot exchange-traded funds for XRP recorded net inflows of $4.07 million on Nov. 25. XRP was the only cryptocurrency among the 10 ETF categories tracked in a SoSoValue snapshot shared by BankXRP to register net inflows.

Wednesday's inflows narrowed the net outflow gap for XRP ETFs. Following the latest inflows, XRP funds had recorded $21.25 million more in investor outflows than inflows over the 30 days ending Nov. 25.

That means the net outflows over the rest of the period totaled $25.32 million. In a single trading day, investors covered about 16% of that shortfall.

The five U.S. spot XRP ETFs tracked by SoSoValue currently have total net assets of $1.04 billion. This is marginally higher than the $1 billion held by nine spot Solana ETFs.

However, there is a larger disparity in cumulative net inflows between XRP and Solana funds. Cumulative net inflows total $1.79 billion for XRP and $1.51 billion for Solana.

The two figures measure different things. Cumulative net inflows represent the total amount of money invested in the funds minus redemptions.

Net assets, on the other hand, represent the current value of a fund's holdings. This figure changes with the price of XRP.

This explains why XRP funds have a little over $1 billion in net assets despite attracting nearly $1.8 billion in cumulative net inflows.

Trading activity was slightly higher in Solana ETFs on Wednesday, with total volume reaching $35.54 million, compared to $33.40 million for XRP.

However, Solana ETFs recorded zero net flows for the day.

Investors can trade existing ETF shares with one another without affecting the total amount of money invested in the funds.

The contrast with Bitcoin ETFs was stark.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $123.41 million in net outflows on Wednesday, according to preliminary figures reported by SoSoValue.

However, the total for Bitcoin was still being compiled when BankXRP shared the numbers. SoSoValue marked the XRP total as complete.

With U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving, XRP ETF buyers have only one more trading day this week.

Trading resumes on U.S. equity markets on Friday, Nov. 27. However, the session will end early, with markets closing at 1 p.m. Eastern time.

#5149. How AI Might Break Crypto: Explaining P vs NP Problem

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

The P vs NP question in computer science pops up in our feeds way more often than it did just a few days ago. No wonder—it's a problem mostly relevant and interesting to mathematicians and computer scientists, and it's also a Clay Millennium Prize problem. It asks a relatively simple question: whether every problem whose solution can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly.

Short answer: no, it can't. P vs NP is an efficiency question. NP is about whether a proposed solution can be checked efficiently, while P covers problems that computers can solve efficiently. For example, solving a complicated Sudoku certainly takes time, but checking the result is not as hard.

The question itself simply asks whether every checkable problem has an efficient solution. P ≠ NP says that some problems are harder to solve than to verify, and that is a core question: most scientists expect P ≠ NP, but proving it is the hard part.

Cryptography is purely mathematical, so issues relevant to computation apply here. ZK-proofs represent a more relevant crypto technology used every day and connected to NP: a statement (such as a transaction) is proven without revealing additional data (a zero-knowledge proof).

But the question is different: could it raise any problems, cause security concerns, or lead to exploits? To some extent—yes. Public-key cryptography is certainly something that can be affected right away—as can blockchains, wallets, and even HTTPS—but P=NP alone wouldn't break the whole industry.

Not really, because you can't change the fundamental math. Even if consensus mechanisms are changed and networks are upgraded, it would be similar to solving 2=2. It's fundamental. But instead of 'solving' it, cryptocurrency projects might adapt to such challenges. New systems might avoid relying on assumptions, so such a change would be a reaction to the consequences.

Quantum computing is a different story. Unlike P vs NP, quantum computing is not just a theoretical question about computational complexity. It's a technological development that could directly affect existing cryptographic systems.

#5148. Why So Many New Moms Are Told to Wait to Exercise Again—and What the Research Really Says

The six-week postpartum checkup was never meant to be about fitness.

Earlier this year, trainer and WH advisory board member Sohee Carpenter, CSCS, posted an Instagram Reel challenging some conventional postpartum advice: Don’t work out until your ob-gyn clears you at your six-week follow-up appointment. Her point wasn’t that new moms should rush back to the gym. It was that one timeline can’t fit everyone. Some women are ready to move sooner, and others need more time.

“I feel like so many people get angry because they assume we mean you're going to be doing a one-rep max back squat a week after you have a baby,” Carpenter says. “But that's definitely not what we're saying.” (By “we,” she means trainers who keep up with the latest research on pregnancy and postpartum exercise.)

The problem, Carpenter explains, is that the six-week rule isn’t based on evidence. On the contrary, research suggests that this type of blanket advice doesn’t make sense for something as personal as postpartum recovery. When you return to exercise after childbirth should depend on your own symptoms, not a date on the calendar.

“There's really nothing magical about the six-week time point,” says Margie Davenport, PhD, a professor of kinesiology at the University of Alberta and chair of the 2025 Canadian Guidelines for Physical Activity for Pregnancy and Postpartum—the first-ever exercise guidelines to specifically focus on evidence-based suggestions for that first year postpartum. In the U.S., the main guidance from the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) covers pregnancy and the postpartum period together. ACOG’s guidance points in the same direction, though: It says many women can start exercising again within days of an uncomplicated birth. In fact, “there is no identified ideal time to return,” Davenport says.

Based on the wide range of comments on Carpenter’s post—some supportive, some hypercritical, and still others asking more questions to try to better understand this shift away from the advice they’ve always heard—there’s still a lot of confusion around postpartum exercise. So we asked experts to break down what the research actually says, and how to approach working out in this new chapter of life.

In many cultures, the first 30 or 40 days postpartum is traditionally considered a protected time to rest, relax, and recover, Davenport says. In Chinese culture, it’s called zuo yuezi, which translates to “sitting the month.” In many Latin American and Latino communities, it’s known as “la cuarentena,” a nod to its roughly 40-day length. In South Korea, it’s sanhujori, or “postpartum care.”

These traditions carry deep cultural significance and are meant to offer real healing and support after birth from one’s community (they put “it takes a village” into practice). They’re rooted in caregiving and cultural custom, and they were never meant to serve as a medical timeline for when it’s safe to start exercising.

In Western medicine, six weeks has become an important medical benchmark in postpartum recovery—and, over time, a default point for returning to exercise too. “At that point, your uterus should be back to its pre-pregnancy state, and so a lot of the gynecologic changes should be fairly reversed by that point,” says Rita Deering, DPT, PhD, associate professor of exercise science and director of the Pelvic Health, Exercise & Musculoskeletal (PHEM) Research Laboratory at Marquette University.

The first six weeks after birth are also when the risk of complications like high blood pressure and infection is highest, Deering says, which is part of why that window became an important medical checkpoint (even though some pregnancy-related changes take longer to resolve). But, she says, “it was never intended to be about exercise.”

So how did six weeks become the exercise rule? Before researchers knew much about how safe it is to exercise during pregnancy and after birth, working out was considered potentially risky, Deering says. There wasn’t strong evidence that exercise wouldn’t slow healing or raise the odds of complications. So the most cautious advice was simply to wait until a doctor confirmed you’d healed enough to resume physical activity.

To come up with the 2025 Canadian Guidelines, researchers did a deep dive of all the available research on the topic, which included 574 unique studies organized into seven systematic reviews based on 21 different outcomes of postpartum exercise—such as depression and anxiety, low-back pain, injuries, glucose and blood pressure levels, and more. They also assembled an international panel of experts to give their recommendations.

Their advice: Start light-intensity physical activity and mobilization (think: carrying your baby around your home, a slow walk down the block, pelvic floor physical therapy) right away. From there, progress as you feel ready to moderate-to-vigorous activity such as brisk walking, resistance training, and running at your own pace—as long as tears and incisions have sufficiently healed and you don’t experience additional bleeding with exercise. (As mentioned, ACOG similarly recommends that women can return to postnatal exercise within days after an uncomplicated birth.)

Based on the research, there are no “absolute contraindications” to exercise postpartum, Davenport says—meaning no condition would rule out exercise entirely. There are some relative contraindications, she explains, “where you might have to delay a little bit or modify the type of activity that you're doing.” Examples include severe abdominal pain, extreme fatigue, and C-section incision pain that worsens with activity. All warrant a conversation with your doctor before starting.

Want to Know More About Lifting While Pregnant? Start Here

Pelvic floor symptoms, like leaking urine or a feeling of heaviness in the vagina, aren’t a reason to stop exercising altogether. If you notice signs of pelvic floor dysfunction, the guidelines recommend starting slowly and building up gradually instead. “Some leakage is okay,” Davenport says. “It means that the training that you’re doing is just overloading the muscle.”

Many people, including plenty of commenters on Carpenter’s Reel, worry that exercising after birth will damage the pelvic floor and cause dysfunction. But the evidence doesn’t support that. In fact, those muscles will likely be better off if you resume training, especially if you do exercises to target them in particular. “Engaging in pelvic floor muscle training reduces your risk of urinary incontinence by around 37 percent,” Davenport says. Additionally, if you stop all exercise because you're leaking a little bit, “this can actually mean that you're missing out on those other benefits.”

One caveat: If you’re leaking a lot, or it’s getting worse over time, “you probably need to pull it back,” Davenport says. That means being more selective about the moves you choose. For example, you might skip long runs and high-impact moves like jump squats for now, adds Sheridan Skye, a registered nurse, pre- and postnatal fitness coach, and founder of The Female Fitness Formula. Stick with lower-impact exercises, then build up gradually as you get stronger and your symptoms level off or improve.

At the end of the day, every body, birth, and recovery is vastly different. “Some people have a very uncomplicated labor and delivery and pregnancy; for others, it's quite complex,” says Davenport. “It only makes sense that the way that they're returning and what time they're actually returning is also going to be quite individualized.”

For some new moms, six weeks is too soon, and a blanket deadline only adds stress. “Maybe they aren't sleeping or they don't have the support to be able to return [to exercise] at six weeks,” Davenport says. On the flip side, for someone who had a straightforward delivery and is itching to get moving again, “telling them to wait for six weeks with no evidence to support it is also inappropriate.”

In fact, exercise can offer significant benefits during postpartum recovery, even before the six-week mark. “It improves muscle and bone density that we lose throughout pregnancy,” Skye says. Postpartum exercise is associated with a 45 percent reduction in the odds of developing postpartum depression, and starting before 12 weeks is even more beneficial.

It’s also associated with a 28 percent reduction in the risk of developing diabetes postpartum. Exercise even improves sleep quality, Skye notes. “Women tend to feel more energized and like they've experienced more rest, even if they haven't,” she says. (Anyone who’s survived a 3 a.m. feeding stretch knows that’s no small thing!)

There is also evidence that exercise in general can help to decrease pain, says Deering, and research links sedentary behavior to lumbopelvic (the areas of the lower back and pelvis) pain. “So if you are having pain, movement might be what you need to help with that.”

For many people, it may be difficult to know if you’re truly ready. “Especially when you're postpartum, it can feel like you are super out of touch with your body sensations, especially if you're not sleeping well,” Carpenter says.

If you're at the point where you're thinking about it, but are nervous or unsure or just overwhelmed by having another decision to make, Davenport recommends taking the Get Active Questionnaire for Postpartum—a tool that her team designed as part of the 2025 guideline. It can help you quickly understand if you’re ready to start from a medical perspective. That can help give you some reassurance.

There can also be “a lot of fear involved,” Carpenter says, especially if you had a C-section or are healing from a vaginal tear. In that case, “you’re probably going to be a bit hesitant,” which is completely understandable. Starting slower and lighter than you think you need to is perfectly fine as you get reacquainted with your body. “The first several sessions are really about mentally trying to get that confidence back,” she says.

As you go, pay attention to how your body responds. Leaking, for instance? That’s not a reason to stop exercising, but you may want to adjust your workout to reduce it. More bleeding, new pain, or a sense that something just doesn’t feel right are signs to stop, reassess, and possibly scale back. If they don’t improve, check in with your doctor. “It’s really about setting your ego aside and being willing to modify, even if it’s one rep to the next, based on how you’re feeling right at that time,” Carpenter says.

And if you feel physically ready but aren’t quite there mentally? “It’s okay to honor those feelings,” Deering says, “and to recognize that it’s okay to give yourself some time.” Whether that’s two weeks, six weeks, or six months, the right moment to start moving is the one that works for you.

XMR fell more than 20% on November 26, briefly touching around $430 after KuCoin announced its delisting.

KuCoin will close four XMR spot markets on November 30, with withdrawals scheduled to remain open until December 31.

MEXC has also removed XMR spot and futures markets, while Eigenwallet's atomic swaps offer another exchange route.

Monero took a sharp hit on November 26, with the KuCoin Monero delisting announcement landing as XMR suffered its biggest single-day decline since June 4.

The timing is hard to ignore. But one exchange announcement doesn’t explain every sell order.

KuCoin confirmed it will close four XMR spot markets “XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC” at 08:00 UTC on November 30.

Other services face separate cutoffs. XMR Flexible Savings ends November 27 at 12:00 UTC, while Convert closes November 30 at 03:00 UTC. Trading bots stop at 06:00 UTC, followed by spot trading at 08:00 UTC.

Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC. Deposits are already closed. KuCoin says open orders will be cancelled when trading ends, while Flexible Savings balances and accrued earnings will move to Funding Accounts.

The exchange also warns withdrawals could be suspended earlier under certain project-related circumstances. It hasn’t provided a detailed reason for the removal.

KuCoin isn’t the only venue cutting Monero access. MEXC previously announced the removal of XMR spot pairs and later issued a separate notice covering XMR and DASH perpetual futures.

Those are different products. Spot markets provide access to the underlying asset, while perpetual contracts offer derivatives exposure.

Earlier Monero research from TRM Labs described liquidity becoming concentrated across fewer venues following exchange restrictions. That context matters, but it doesn’t establish how much of Thursday’s sell-off came from KuCoin.

Monero’s official account also announced an Eigenwallet release supporting Bitcoin and Monero, including native atomic swaps. These swaps allow users to exchange the assets without depositing both with a conventional exchange.

Still, a new trading route doesn’t automatically replace the depth of removed order books. The KuCoin Monero delisting leaves XMR facing a practical liquidity question as the deadlines approach.

A Zcash (ZEC) whale that bought 23,412 ZEC nine years ago moved 15,750 ZEC worth $11.39 million after nine years of inactivity, Lookonchain reported on Thursday. According to Lookonchain, the whale paid $5.04 million for the coins at an average price of $215.

Lookonchain also said that after nine years of holding, the whale was finally selling, and that his total profit on the position was more than $12 million.

Arkham data shows that the whale sent the ZEC in two transactions. The first one, 8,000 ZEC worth $5.73 million, went to an address without an Arkham label. About an hour later, the wallet sent 7,750 ZEC worth $5.66 million to a Kraken deposit address.

The whale got the coins nine years ago from Zcash's shielded pool. He withdrew most of them in batches of 250 ZEC, according to Arkham.

On Thursday, Lookonchain also reported that another whale deposited about 47,500 ZEC, or $35.8 million, to Binance.

ZEC dropped as low as $675.67 over the past 24 hours and was trading at $748.87 on Thursday, according to CoinGecko. CoinGecko put the market capitalization of ZEC at $12.77 billion, which made it the 11th-largest cryptocurrency. On Nov. 18, the price of ZEC was around $927.

A day before that, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes set a $1,800 target for ZEC with no deadline. Hayes put Zcash in a group of four tokens that he called the "Four Horsemen," together with Ethereum, NEAR and Venice Token.

"The Four Horsemen shall pump and then usher in the end of the AI bubble," Hayes wrote on X. According to Hayes, the size of his position is "small to medium as conviction is meh."

Bitwise filed an S-1 for a Zcash ETF on Nov. 17 as well. The filing shows that the fund would trade on the Texas Stock Exchange under the ticker ZEC and would not use staking or shielded transactions.

On Thursday, Zakura, the Zcash development team led by Sean Bowe and Dev Ojha, asked users to move their ZEC out of the Sapling pool. Zcash launched Sapling in October 2018, and according to Zakura, about 400,000 ZEC still sits in it.

On Nov. 18, 2020, the Canopy upgrade at block 1,046,400 stopped new deposits into Sprout, Zcash's first shielded pool, according to the Electric Coin Company. Zcash activated its latest upgrade, NU7, at block 3,543,405 on Nov. 6. According to ZIP 218, NU7 cut the target block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.

"Practical pairing breaks are highly speculative," Zakura wrote about the cryptography behind Sapling.

#5145. Ripple News: XRP Price Tries to Reclaim $1 Again – But Will The Breakout Survive the Weekend?

Ripple news: XRP climbs 3.6% toward $1 as RLUSD hits a record supply and ETF inflows return. Can XRP finally break resistance?

XRP is approaching a price level it has repeatedly failed to reclaim. According to the latest Ripple news, the token climbed 3.6% to $0.978 on November 27, putting $1 back within reach for the sixth time in two weeks.

The token has a busy week of Ripple updates behind it. Ripple signed a Turkish bank as a custody client, and its RLUSD stablecoin reached a record supply. Spot XRP ETFs, which hold the token itself, drew fresh money. XRP Ledger validators also moved closer to switching on a lending feature.

JUST IN: Ripple’s lending proposal is one validator vote from $XRP Ledger approval, potentially unlocking lending for its $837 million stablecoin market. pic.twitter.com/jB5a4RYAlK

— Whale Insider (@WhaleInsider) November 27, 2026

XRP needs the help. It is down 56% from a year ago and has lost more than a fifth of its value since the start of November.

The question is whether this Ripple news is enough to push XRP back through $1. Our check of the daily chart shows why the level matters so much.

The largest piece of Ripple news came on Wednesday. Ripple announced that Yapı Kredi, one of Türkiye’s largest private banks, will use Ripple Custody to hold crypto for its trading arm. The system runs on the bank’s own premises. Ripple says its technology now sits behind every leading Turkish bank licensed as a crypto custodian, and that the company holds more than 85 licenses worldwide.

Ripple’s stablecoin is growing too. RLUSD’s supply reached a record of about $2.85 billion this week across Ethereum and the XRP Ledger, making it the fifth-largest stablecoin.

Fund demand is returning, slowly. US spot XRP ETFs took in $4.07 million on Tuesday, the only crypto ETF group with inflows that day. The five funds hold $1.04 billion in total, though they are still $21 million in the red over the past 30 days.

On the XRP Ledger, the network that XRP runs on, validators are close to approving a bank-style lending system. A vault feature could go live on December 9. The lending upgrade, which validators must vote on, is one vote short of the support it needs.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

To see why $1 matters, we went through XRP’s daily candles on Binance since June.

The level held XRP up for most of the summer. XRP touched $1 in late June and again for two weeks in August, and buyers stepped in each time. After a brief dip in mid-August, it then closed above $1 for 89 days in a row, from August 17 to November 13.

That streak ended on November 14, when XRP fell 10% in a day. Since then the old floor has acted as a ceiling. XRP’s daily high reached or came within a cent of $1 on November 14, 17, 18, 19 and 23, and every time sellers pushed it back. The highest attempt, on Monday, briefly hit $1.026 before XRP closed at $0.94.

Binance’s order book shows the wall too. On Friday afternoon, sell orders worth about $700,000 sat at $1.00, more than double the orders at $0.99.

LayerZero's Zero mainnet launch and new institutional validators could strengthen ecosystem adoption and investor interest in the ZRO price.

ZRO remains in a descending channel, with weakening OBV highlighting selling pressure and the need to defend the demand zone.

LayerZero’s native token, ZRO, is approaching a crucial milestone as it trades near $1.10, up approximately 1.12% in the past 24 hours. The upcoming November 30 launch of its Zero mainnet has renewed investor attention, with new validators and trading platforms joining the ecosystem ahead of the rollout.

However, ZRO’s price continues to struggle within a prolonged descending channel, raising questions about whether this major launch can finally reverse its bearish trajectory. With the token hovering near its demand zone and the launch just days away, investors are watching whether the November 30 event can trigger a meaningful recovery or expose ZRO to further downside.

With the November 30 Zero mainnet launch approaching, LayerZero is adding more established names to its ecosystem. On November 25, the protocol announced that Kakao Pay, Samsung Card and ZAN would join Zero as genesis validators. Their involvement will help support the network’s initial operations, including consensus and proof verification. Kakao Pay is also exploring the possibility of using Zero’s infrastructure for a Korean won-backed stablecoin ecosystem, although no launch has been confirmed.

LayerZero is also expanding its cross-chain capabilities. On November 12, Flare announced its integration with the protocol as a Decentralized Verifier Network (DVN). This will allow Flare to help verify messages transferred between blockchains, initially supporting Flare and Ethereum. The integration is expected to go live in early December.

Another development worth watching is ZRO staking, which opened on November 23. Token holders can now stake their holdings to support Zero’s initial validator network. However, there is a catch: staked tokens will remain locked until March 31, 2027, with an additional withdrawal cooldown of up to seven days. Together, these developments show that LayerZero is building out its infrastructure and bringing more participants into the ecosystem ahead of launch.

ZRO continues to face selling pressure on the weekly chart, with the token trading around $1.109 after declining 7.12% during the week. The latest pullback follows an unsuccessful recovery towards $2 to $2.3, suggesting that buyers are struggling to sustain upward momentum. More importantly, ZRO remains confined within a descending parallel channel that has guided its price movement since early 2025.

The On-Balance Volume (OBV) indicator is also showing signs of weakening demand. Its latest reading stands at approximately 389.4 million, after retreating from a recent peak above 500 million. This decline suggests that selling volume has been outweighing buying volume during the latest pullback. The weekly chart also highlights an important demand zone around 0.70–1.10, where ZRO is currently trading. Holding this region could provide a base for another recovery attempt. However, a sustained breakdown below the lower boundary of the descending channel would expose the token to further downside.

On the upside, the descending channel’s upper boundary remains an important hurdle. A breakout would need to be followed by a move above the $2.97 to $3.16 resistance zone, which has previously acted as a significant supply area. Beyond this, the next major order-block region lies between $4.90 and $6.00.

LayerZero’s November 30 Zero mainnet launch could improve market sentiment, supported by new institutional validators and ecosystem integrations. However, ZRO’s weekly chart remains bearish, with declining OBV indicating weakening buying pressure. For now, the mainnet launch is a potential catalyst, but ZRO’s price needs stronger buying volume and a breakout to confirm a trend reversal.

#5143. New Bitcoin Core Update: Breaking Down the Details

The key reason behind the setup is error handling in a way where there's no break in wallet usage that needs manual intervention in the process, to a significant degree. Indeed, a Bitcoin wallet migration change was, broadly speaking, merged on November 25 by Bitcoin Core.

The pull request follows two earlier fixes, one for unnamed legacy wallets and another for crashes when Bitcoin Core couldn't write to the wallet directory, on the whole. In fact, the thinking is to handle failures in a controlled way so the process can (to some degree) automatically restore the original wallet without needing manual intervention.

This isn't the first fix for wallet migration either, in the actual application.

Some mismatches during wallet creation could crash the graphical app or cause it to return a generic error. Those differences are now caught by Bitcoin Core and reported, which lets the migration process restore the original wallet from its backup, There are a couple of cases where the process could abruptly stop.

Trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory could also throw an error and skip cleanup, in real-world scenarios. In fact, now the process crashes with a clear error message. The test for this case is checking that the wallet is still in the old database format after the failure.

The biggest change is in how Bitcoin Core moves the wallet to SQLite. Earlier, it deleted the original database before writing the new one. If something went wrong while making the new database or writing the wallet records, the user could end up restoring the backup by hand.

Now Bitcoin Core builds the SQLite database next to the original. So, the old database stays in place. These days, the new one is being built. Once the wallet records have been written successfully, Bitcoin Core can move the new database into place. The pull request also tests this with a wallet stored on a separate filesystem.

A leftover SQLite journal in the wallet directory can corrupt the new database if SQLite uses it for the migrated wallet. In fact, Bitcoin Core now stops the migration when it finds a file, and the test checks that the journal stays in place. Moreover, the wallet keeps its legacy format.

It's significant to keep in mind that automatic recovery still hinges on the backup being copied back successfully. As Ryan Ofsky mentioned in his review, if that copy crashes, the user still has to restore the backup by hand, on the whole.

#5142. Bitcoin Network Activity Surges Despite Whales Dumping 150K BTC as Price Slump Deepens

Bitcoin’s network activity continues to show signs of resilience despite mounting price pressure.

According to leading on-chain analytics provider Santiment, Bitcoin is creating about 50,000 new addresses per day, showing accelerating network growth despite the market downturn.

Tether’s USDT on Ethereum is also experiencing increased adoption, adding roughly 25,000 new addresses over the past month.

Therefore, this simultaneous growth is encouraging given the broader market weakness.

Why is this the case? Well, Bitcoin’s expanding address count points to rising network participation, while USDT’s growth illustrates continued activity in trading, payments, and capital transfers across the crypto ecosystem.

If both networks maintain this momentum through the final weeks of 2026, there is light at the end of the tunnel since it could strengthen the foundation for a more sustainable market recovery heading into 2027.

In a concerning twist, Santiment also revealed that wallets holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC have collectively offloaded approximately 150,000 BTC, representing a 1.1% reduction in their holdings since November 2.

Over the same period, Bitcoin dropped by 24.5%, sliding from $76,700 to $57,900.

Why is this development worth a keen eye? Well, sharks and whales still control 67.55% of Bitcoin’s circulating supply, making their investment decisions particularly influential.

Therefore, continued distribution from this group could increase selling pressure and undermine attempts at a sustained recovery.

According to Santiment, a stabilization in their collective holdings around 13.58 million BTC, followed by renewed accumulation, would improve the prospects of a more convincing relief rally.

From the price action front, the top cryptocurrency recently rebounded to the $60,000 zone, thanks to renewed market optimism following Nvidia’s announcement concerning Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO and president, with the current price being $59,805 per CoinGecko data.

Nevertheless, Bitcoin is not out of the woods yet since its next four-year cycle bottom could form around $41,000. Therefore, time will tell how the apex cryptocurrency plays out in the short term.

Working up a sweat feels great, but staying drenched in a sweaty shirt post-workout really doesn’t. That’s where moisture-wicking shirts designed to handle your sweat sessions come in. I tested them during sweaty workouts, walking workouts, and even on errand days. After months of testing, I, along with a few other fitness experts, chose options that checked off all our boxes.

The Smartwool Active Mesh Short Sleeve was hands-down the best moisture-wicking shirt we tested over the past few months—and for good reason. It’s super lightweight, breathable, has a relaxed fit, and is made with merino wool, which helps keep you cool no matter how intense your workout gets.

This is one of my go-to tops for working out or running errands. SingleAssetVault activation is projected for December 9, subject to continued validator support.

XRPL stablecoin supply reached $836.90 million, with RLUSD representing 89.35%.

The proposed lending system supports uncollateralised loans, while borrower underwriting remains offchain.

The XRP Ledger lending system is getting closer to deployment, but don’t confuse a countdown with a working loan market. The SingleAssetVault amendment is projected to activate on December 9, provided validator support holds. The separate LendingProtocol amendment still needs approval.

Meanwhile, XRPL stablecoin supply has reached $836.90 million. RLUSD accounts for 89.35% of that total, according to November 27 figures. That’s a sizeable balance, but it isn’t money already committed to lending.

The SingleAssetVault amendment would establish infrastructure for pooling a single asset and issuing depositors shares representing their interest. The LendingProtocol amendment performs a different job: it enables brokers to arrange fixed-term loans and record repayments on the ledger.

XRPL amendments need more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks. If support falls short, the waiting period can restart. So December 9 remains a projection, not a guaranteed launch date.

The proposed system supports uncollateralised loans, making borrower assessment a serious issue for depositors. Underwriting and risk management happen offchain, according to the lending specification.

Brokers may also contribute optional first-loss capital in the same asset as the loan pool. That can absorb some missed-payment losses, but it isn’t a blanket guarantee.

The XRP Ledger Foundation has published an open-source reference application demonstrating the system on Devnet. It combines vaults and lending with credentials, permissioned domains and batch transactions.

Still, a working demonstration isn’t commercial adoption. XRPL DeFi total value locked stands at about $30.65 million, a separate measure from the $836.94 million stablecoin balance.

The XRP Ledger lending system now needs amendment activation, production markets and funded loans before stablecoin supply can translate into actual lending activity.

Coinbase has suspended trading for 12 crypto trading pairs, including those of Cardano (ADA) and Stellar (XLM), as November 2026 wraps up with just a few days left.

The delisting took place on November 25, as Coinbase announced earlier. The affected pairs include APE-USDT, ATOM-USDT, ALGO-BTC, CRV-BTC, ETC-BTC, XLM-BTC, ICP-BTC, and ADA-ETH, among others.

The full list includes APE-USDT, ATOM-USDT, ALGO-BTC, CRV-BTC, ETC-BTC, ICP-BTC, XLM-BTC, APE-EUR, ADA-ETH, 1INCH-GBP, CHZ-GBP, and SNX-GBP, with trading suspended across Coinbase Exchange, Advanced Trade and Coinbase Prime.

Coinbase regularly monitors the markets on the exchange and, in an effort to improve overall market health and consolidate liquidity, has removed a number of non-USD trading pairs for supported assets.

In similar delisting news, Coinbase has disabled trading for Stargate Finance (STG), Vulcan Forged (PYR), Neon EVM (NEON), and Syndicate (SYND), in line with the shake-up on its platform in November. Users' funds will remain accessible, and users will be able to withdraw them at any time.

As stated earlier, Coinbase regularly monitors the markets on the exchange and might delist some assets to improve overall market health and consolidate liquidity.

Based on recent reviews, Coinbase will suspend trading for Centrifuge (CFG) on December 18, 2026, at or around 2 PM ET. Centrifuge has separately announced it is ending token support for CFG and allowing holders to convert CFG tokens into equity in Centrifuge.

Also in December, Coinbase will be performing a system upgrade. In an X post, the exchange stated it has scheduled a system upgrade for Saturday, December 5, 2026, around 7 a.m. PT, estimated to last about 4 hours.

During this time, Coinbase stated that all trading and transfers will be unavailable, and the Coinbase Exchange will be temporarily offline. Users are advised to take note and prepare accordingly so as to avoid any delays on that date.

The recovery follows a difficult stretch, as Bitcoin still remains down over 20% in November (its largest monthly decline since June), and US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded monthly outflows of $5.39 billion. The Fear and Greed Index sits at 11, signaling extreme fear, and roughly $7 billion in Bitcoin options expired earlier today with traders positioned defensively. Total crypto market capitalization stands near $2.1 trillion, up 1.09% on the day, with Bitcoin’s own market cap at $1.23 trillion.

While prices stabilize and caution lingers, the BTC Layer 2 project Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) has closed its presale, which raised $33.3 million since it began in May last year. Participants are now able to claim their HYPER tokens, which can also be traded on the top DEX platforms Uniswap and Raydium. Bitcoin Hyper’s strong raise and timely token generation event highlight sustained interest in infrastructure that can expand Bitcoin’s practical uses, setting the stage for the project’s next development steps.

Bitcoin Hyper (HYPER) is aiming to be the fastest true Bitcoin Layer 2 network. It integrates the Solana Virtual Machine to deliver high throughput and low latency, allowing near-instant Bitcoin transactions at minimal cost while settling security back to Bitcoin’s Layer 1. Users deposit native BTC into a Canonical Bridge, which verifies Bitcoin block headers and transaction proofs before minting equivalent wrapped BTC on the Layer 2.

That wrapped BTC can then move freely for payments, decentralized finance activity, staking, and on-chain applications. Withdrawals reverse the process, returning BTC to the user’s Layer 1 address after state verification.

The HYPER token functions as the network’s native utility asset. It covers gas fees for transfers and smart-contract interactions, supports staking for rewards, and grants access to advanced features and governance participation. Token allocations direct 20% to marketing, 15% to rewards, 30% to development, 25% to the project’s treasury, and 10% to major exchange listings.

Hyper Mainnet is now secured by @hackenclub 🔓 ⚡

Final Report: https://t.co/nSJy3Ys8mY pic.twitter.com/zY1ahvp7dQ

— Bitcoin Hyper (@BTC_Hyper2) November 26, 2026

The Bitcoin Hyper network’s architecture relies on a hybrid design (audited by Hacken), in which the Layer 2 handles execution via the Solana Virtual Machine and a Proof-of-Stake validator set, while Bitcoin’s Proof-of-Work system provides periodic anchoring for state integrity.

The completed HYPER presale, which drew $33.3 million, shows clear demand for these capabilities. With the token generation event now finished, buyers can access their allocations as the project moves forward with its Layer 2 deployment timeline.

The Bitcoin Hyper claiming process begins on the project’s official website. Users should first hard-refresh the page to clear the cache, then connect the same wallet employed during the presale. Two options will be available: a standard claim or a claim-and-stake choice.

Solana purchases will need to be claimed on Solana with the original wallet; Ethereum, BSC, or credit-card purchases can be claimed only on Ethereum. Credit card buyers can locate the registered wallet address on their Wert receipt.

Best Wallet holders can claim directly through the app’s Upcoming Tokens section; mobile users should also get smoother results by opening the site inside the wallet’s built-in browser. The project recommends keeping $10–20 worth of ETH or SOL on hand for gas fees incurred during the claim process.

The team will never request private keys or seed phrases, and claims can be completed only through the official site or through Best Wallet. A full guide to claiming HYPER has been published on X via the official Bitcoin Hyper account.

Full claim instructions on the official Hyper TG 👇https://t.co/iukXzZWfcX pic.twitter.com/6SneDFHPBO

HYPER is available for trading on Uniswap and Raydium. Staked tokens become claimable starting December 3, and any tokens staked after the presale ends will be claimable exactly seven days later. The project is continuing its progress toward the Layer 2 mainnet launch on December 3, when staked allocations unlock and additional network components go live.

This sequence keeps Bitcoin Hyper on track to broaden Bitcoin’s utility through faster settlement and expanded application support, reinforcing a positive outlook for the token as the leading cryptocurrency’s everyday functionality expands.

Two XRP Ledger lending amendments, LendingProtocol and LendingProtocolV1_1, each have 28 votes out of 35 validators, or 80%, according to XRPScan data on Thursday. Each of them needs one more vote to start a 14-day countdown to activation, according to XRPScan.

On Wednesday, the SingleAssetVault amendment reached 29 votes. According to XRPScan, its earliest activation date is Dec. 9, and its support has to stay above 80% until then.

XRP was trading at around $0.95 on Thursday, up 4.1% over 24 hours, according to CoinMarketCap.

On Nov. 20, XRPScan showed 25 votes for SingleAssetVault and 24 votes for each of the two lending amendments. Validators run by Interledger, onXRP, GateHub and Flare were among the last to vote for them.

RippleX opened LendingProtocolV1_1 for voting with a post on X on Sept. 30, when the amendment arrived with rippled version 3.4.0. "LendingProtocolV1_1 is open for validator voting. It introduces closed-ended vaults and cash-basis accounting for XRPL lending, and it must activate before LendingProtocol and SingleAssetVault can proceed," the RippleX developer account wrote.

J. Ayo Akinyele, head of engineering at RippleX, explained the role of the update in a post on June 25. "v1.1 is an enhancement to the Lending Protocol, not a replacement for v1.0," he wrote, adding that "Lending on XRPL will evolve dynamically."

Ripple described the mechanics of the protocol on Nov. 19. "The upcoming XRP Ledger Lending Protocol is designed to bring loan issuance and repayment directly onto the ledger. Lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital to issue loans and track repayments onchain," the company wrote on X.

Ripple engineer Ed Hennis presented the protocol in a thread on X in December 2025. He called it a protocol-native system for "fixed-term, fixed-rate, underwritten credit." "XRP's $124B market cap can finally be lent into institutional credit facilities to generate real yield instead of sitting idle," Hennis wrote at the time.

Jazzi Cooper, head of product at RippleX, wrote on Sept. 11 that "XRP as collateral for institutional credit is a killer use case (and supported by xls65/66 lending protocol!)"

On the same day, the XRP Ledger Foundation shared an interview with its chief technology officer, Denis Angell. "We are writing TradFi primitives into the XRP Ledger," Angell said. In the interview, he compared the lending protocol to a closed-end fund, where investors put in XRP or RLUSD and receive interest.

BlackRock’s investors have sold cryptocurrencies worth more than $22 billion so far in November 2026, despite cumulative positive fundamentals.

As of Friday, November 27, BlackRock had offloaded crypto assets worth approximately $22.36 billion, according to data Coinpedia fetched from Arkham Intelligence, a blockchain analytics platform.

As a result, the firm’s crypto portfolio had $48.81 billion, down from $71.17 billion recorded at the beginning of the month.

BlackRock investors sold Bitcoin (BTC) worth $19.33 billion over the past three weeks, down from $63.85 billion on November 1 to $44.51 billion at the time of reporting. During the last 24 hours, BTC’s average trading volume had spiked by 18.82% to $31.62 billion.

As BlackRock accelerated its ETH selloff in November, Ethereum price capitulated by 28.76% to trade at $1,669.20. On Friday, the leading altcoin saw its average 24-hour trading volume drop by over 29% to $11.6 billion.

#5134. XRP Exchange Outflows Hit 5 Billion as Price Rebounds

XRP has seen traders withdraw large amounts of tokens out of major crypto exchanges, especially Binance, over the last 30 days even as the broad market volatility persists.

Despite the intense selling pressure XRP has witnessed over the past few months, data from the crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant shows that XRP’s exchange outflow has reached 5 billion XRP over the last month.

While the massive 30-day exchange outflow of 5 billion XRP is a relief signal because it signals persistent demand for XRP even amid the intense volatility, further data shows that the outflow is relatively low compared to levels seen in October.

Although the 5 billion XRP outflow is significant and November has yet to wrap up, the data shows that it marks a decent decrease from October, when total exchange outflows for the month reached about 5.7 billion XRP.

Despite the 700,000 XRP decrease in the metric, the outflows registered in the last 30 days are still considered substantial and have drawn attention from market analysts as they signal strong investor conviction even as XRP suffered larger price losses this month compared with October.

Usually, increases in the exchange outflow of an asset suggest that investors are moving assets off exchanges into external wallets, most likely to hold them for longer periods.

Hence, this metric provides a bullish signal for XRP as it indicates strong demand among traders, putting Binance in the spotlight as over a billion XRP were withdrawn from the exchange during the period.

While OKX and Bybit saw traders withdraw 865.27 million XRP and 697.65 million XRP from their platforms, respectively, Binance registered the highest XRP withdrawals, with about 1.439 billion XRP leaving its exchange over the period.

#5133. XRP Updates: The Ambitious Projects That Contribute to Its Widespread Adoption

XRP has earned a reputation as one of the fastest and lowest-cost cryptocurrencies for payments, powered by the XRP Ledger. The Ripple company, under which both technologies thrive, has positioned itself as a tool for companies that want to modernize their infrastructure and approach decentralization effortlessly. The platform supports more than 1,000,000 custody wallets, enabling […]

XRP has earned a reputation as one of the fastest and lowest-cost cryptocurrencies for payments, powered by the XRP Ledger. The Ripple company, under which both technologies thrive, has positioned itself as a tool for companies that want to modernize their infrastructure and approach decentralization effortlessly.

The platform supports more than 1,000,000 custody wallets, enabling users to settle in 3 to 5 seconds. Crypto businesses, payment services providers, and FinTechs can leverage Ripple’s payment system, so use cases are numerous and convincing for investors to buy XRP.

The popularity and growing interest have contributed to the project’s expansion, including securing additional licenses, extending its escrow functionality, and exploring the possibility of native XRP staking, according to the latest news. A lot is going on in the Ripple ecosystem, so let’s explore more about these additions.

The ledger is known for its high performance, low cost, and appeal for streamlined development, making it the perfect option for business use. That’s what the latest upgrade is about, the “Permissioned DEX”. According to the project documentation, the upgrade will allow regulated institutions to manage traded venues on-chain or benefit from a controlled version of the XRPL decentralized exchange.

The supposed administrators of the venues can delegate trades by checking who can place and accept them, which supports a members-only marketplace for different organizations. This will be possible in accordance with compliance requirements, including KYC (Know Your Customer) and AML (Anti-Money Laundering) procedures.

The benefits of this update include increased liquidity and a blockchain-based settlement system, enabling companies to better manage counterparty eligibility. Moreover, users can benefit from the ledgers’ security, but access to information will be restricted accordingly.

When it comes to official banks using XRP, the EU isn’t necessarily the leading region; Asia-Pacific is the leading region. However, this will change soon, as Ripple has received an important approval from the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority for its EMI (Electronic Money Institution) license.

The announcement was soon followed by another approval by Luxembourg’s financial regulator, CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier). Both regulations strengthen Ripple’s trust across Europe by demonstrating the company’s willingness to operate in accordance with comprehensive digital asset regulations.

Ripple has expanded its regulatory footprint to over 75 licenses globally, and the platform now supports more than 90% of daily foreign exchange markets. Therefore, it is ready to lead the global industry into the next era of financial innovation by securing both compliant operations and advanced technologies such as blockchain.

Hyperliquid is one of the fastest-growing decentralized exchanges, with its own blockchain and specializing in perpetual futures trading. Its low fees, favorable leverage levels, and a vast array of assets have made the decentralized exchange an innovative tool in the industry, and Ripple eyed its potential for collaboration.

By integrating Hyperliquid into its prime brokerage platform, Ripple offered institutional customers the chance to leverage on-chain derivatives liquidity while accessing numerous asset classes, from crypto to foreign exchange. The efforts mark the start of a new trend that addresses decentralized exchanges supporting all sorts of assets.

Of course, the collaboration increased the value of Hyperliquid’s native token, HYPE, making it more efficient for users to transact on the blockchain. However, XRP also saw a boost in value following the announcement, showcasing the power of industry collaborations.

The native token of XRPL has seen considerable appreciation for its transaction benefits, but its journey has also faced challenges. Ripple’s court case with the SEC left a question mark regarding the company’s commitment to the global business sector, despite Ripple’s victory after five years of proceedings.

The SEC accused Ripple of facilitating the sale of unregistered securities, which sparked endless disputes over what cryptocurrencies truly are and what the SEC’s stance is on crypto technology. XRP also saw lower prices during this period due to reduced interest in a company facing court cases. In the meantime, the SEC’s management also changed with a more crypto-oriented approach.

Besides these issues, Ripple has continued to expand and is thriving, leading us to believe the future will follow a similar path. Considering the growing number of collaborations with other industry companies and the interest in advanced technological tooling, Ripple might become a competitive brand in the future of Web3.

While the price of XRP still hasn’t reached the heights of Bitcoin or Ethereum, it still has the potential to be useful for real-world cases. As one of the largest coins by market capitalization, XRP is slowly but steadily being adopted by brands that want to offer users the option to pay with crypto, especially since it operates at fast speeds and low fees.

Therefore, XRP is a suitable investment for a diversified portfolio, as it’s supported by active real-world integration and a global user base. As experts forecast rising prices and expanded adoption in the future, investing in it can help build a stable, reliable long-term portfolio.

For those who don’t want to buy the actual coin and only benefit from exposure, they can invest in XRP ETFs, as several SEC-approved ETFs are available on the market from Grayscale or 21Shares. Each listing has different fees, but they may change. In addition, more XRP ETFs will launch in the future as new funds are launched.

XRP is one of the most controversial cryptocurrencies due to its court case with the SEC, but this hasn’t fully affected the brand and its efficiency. Following the victory over the SEC, XRP continued to expand its use cases and collaborations to better support future adoption. For example, some of the latest additions to the Ripple ecosystem include new regulations in the EU and a partnership with a decentralized exchange.

As the total number of burn transactions approaches the 22,000 mark, Shiba Inu’s token-burning activity is nearing another significant milestone.

This is a testament to the continuing efforts by the SHIB community to reduce the cryptocurrency’s massive circulating supply by sending tokens to unreachable wallet addresses. The tokens are sent to these dead wallets and are then permanently out of circulation.

Shiba Inu began with an initial supply of approximately one quadrillion tokens. Since then, over 410.8 trillion SHIB tokens have been burned, meaning that 41.08% of the original supply of 1 quadrillion tokens has been destroyed. But individual burns have very different effects. Some transactions are for relatively small amounts, while others remove millions or even billions of SHIB from circulation.

The milestone is another sign of the community’s ongoing interest in Shiba Inu’s tokenomics as investors look for developments that could create stronger demand across the ecosystem.

The daily burn rate of Shiba Inu has seen a huge spike of 443%, as the SHIB community continues its attempt to shrink the circulating supply of the cryptocurrency.

A higher burn rate indicates more tokens have been destroyed than on the previous day. According to Shibburn, 4.40 million SHIB have been burned in the last 24 hours, with the daily burn rate jumping 443%. This contributes to a total of 8.42 million SHIB burned in the last seven days and 322.85 million SHIB sent to dead wallets in the last 30 days.

Despite these cumulative burns, SHIB’s price performance still depends on broader market conditions and investor demand. At the time of writing, SHIB was up 5.60% in the last 24 hours to $0.00000364 amid the Thanksgiving holiday and down 6.45% weekly.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Shiba Inu (SHIB) met Thanksgiving Day with a "Bull" label on its four-hour price chart. The label appeared on the relative strength index (RSI) of the SHIB/USD chart on TradingView, and on Thursday afternoon SHIB was trading at around $0.00000364, up 1.4% on the day.

On Saturday, SHIB fell as low as $0.00000337, according to TradingView. It was the lowest price of SHIB since 2021, and before that, the lowest price of SHIB in 2026 was $0.00000411 at the July 17 close. On Wednesday, the token dropped close to the Saturday low again. According to the chart, the RSI was around 23 on Saturday and around 32 on Wednesday, and the "Bull" label appeared next to the Wednesday reading.

The Crypto Fear and Greed Index on CoinMarketCap showed 13 on Wednesday, up from 10 on Tuesday.

The four-hour SHIB chart also showed the label on Oct. 27 and Nov. 5. It appeared twice more between Nov. 17 and Nov. 19, and two days later SHIB fell to its Saturday low.

The daily SHIB chart had the same label in late June and in July. On Thursday, there was no new label on the daily chart.

SHIB has lost 22.7% in November so far, according to CryptoRank data as of Nov. 22. The token also lost 29.6% and 24.8% in November of 2021 and 2022, respectively. In November of 2023 and 2024, SHIB gained 6.62% and 48.8%, and last November it fell 16.2%.

SHIB's median December return is -17.6%, and its average December return is -11.4%, according to CryptoRank data. SHIB gained 24.6% in December 2023 and lost 21% and 17.6% in December of 2024 and 2025, respectively. In 2026, SHIB has lost value in six of 11 months so far. In July, August and September, the token gained 12.2%, 7.55% and 13.5%, respectively. SHIB lost 24% in June and 18.6% in October.

On Jan. 1, SHIB closed at $0.00000692, according to CoinGecko. SHIB set its record high of $0.00008845 on Oct. 28, 2021, and in December of that year it lost 29.5%, according to CryptoRank. In January 2022, the token lost another 36%.

The number of SHIB holders on Ethereum passed 1.7 million on Nov. 17, according to Etherscan. CryptoQuant data from that day showed about 312 billion SHIB leaving exchanges.

On Thursday, SHIB was No. 34 on CoinMarketCap with a market capitalization of $2.14 billion. Its circulating supply stood at 589.23 trillion SHIB. Bittensor (TAO) was one place higher, and its market capitalization was also $2.14 billion. Hedera (HBAR) was No. 31 at $2.37 billion, and the PayPal USD (PYUSD) stablecoin held the 32nd spot between them.
