#5106. Zcash Developers Race to Secure Crypto. Can Quantum Computing Break Bitcoin?

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Can quantum computing break crypto? For years, the question has largely been treated as a problem for the distant future. Zcash developers, however, are already discussing what to do with hundreds of thousands of coins that could become vulnerable if certain cryptographic protections fail.

A day earlier, Shielded Labs published its first technical update on a separate project designed to protect Zcash against future quantum computers.

Neither development means cryptocurrency has been cracked. Together, however, they raise a more pressing question: can blockchain developers replace the mathematics protecting investors’ money before someone finds a way around it?

Quantum computing is a way of processing information using the properties of quantum mechanics. Unlike conventional computers, which represent information using bits with a value of either zero or one, quantum computers operate using quantum bits, commonly known as qubits.

By manipulating these qubits, researchers can design algorithms capable of solving certain mathematical problems far more efficiently than conventional computers.

The important word here is certain. A quantum computer is not simply a faster version of the laptop sitting on your desk. Its advantages depend on the type of problem it is trying to solve.

Unfortunately for the cryptocurrency industry, some of those problems underpin the security of digital wallets.

As explained in NewsBTC’s guide to quantum computing, blockchains rely on cryptographic signatures to establish ownership and authorize transactions. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer could undermine some of the signature systems currently used to protect digital assets.

When you send Bitcoin from your wallet, the network needs to establish that you have the authority to spend those coins. It does this by verifying a digital signature produced using your private key.

Your private key is supposed to remain secret. The corresponding public key can be disclosed because working backward from a public key to its private counterpart is computationally impractical using conventional methods.

In 1994, mathematician Peter Shor introduced a quantum algorithm that could efficiently solve certain mathematical problems underlying modern public-key cryptography.

A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running such an algorithm could potentially recover private keys from exposed public keys. An attacker could then create a transaction that the blockchain would recognize as valid, even though the original owner had never authorized it.

That is a particularly uncomfortable problem for cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin does not have a customer service department that can reverse an unauthorized transfer.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology has already developed alternative cryptographic standards intended to withstand these future attacks. The challenge for crypto is incorporating such protection into networks that were originally built around different assumptions.

Bitcoin’s public transaction history makes it possible to estimate how much of its supply could be exposed under certain quantum attack scenarios.

According to a November 25 snapshot from The Quantum Ledger, approximately 7.23 million BTC, representing 35.9% of issued supply under its methodology, was associated with public keys or spending scripts already visible on the blockchain.

Around 1.94 million BTC was classified as exposed because of its output design. A further 5.29 million BTC was associated with addresses that had previously revealed relevant spending information.

Some of these coins date back to Bitcoin’s earliest years, when transactions commonly revealed public keys directly.

Estimates vary between researchers because they do not all measure exposure in exactly the same way. In May 2026, Glassnode’s research identified 6.04 million BTC under its own classification framework.

These figures should not be interpreted as the amount of Bitcoin that will eventually be stolen. They measure a potential vulnerability under a specific future scenario, not an active attack.

Owners of many exposed coins could migrate their holdings if suitable protection becomes available. Dormant wallets whose owners have lost their private keys present a considerably harder problem.

Zcash offers a useful example of how complicated a cryptographic migration can become.

Sapling is one of the network’s older shielded systems. Its proof mechanism relies on mathematical assumptions that Zakura believes warrant additional scrutiny in light of potentially accelerating cryptographic research.

The time to prepare for a cryptographic breakthrough is before it happens.

The amount involved is already changing. A November 27 snapshot from the Zcash Dashboard, timestamped 06:06 UTC, showed approximately 306,684 ZEC remaining in Sapling, below the rounded estimate cited in Zakura’s proposal. The difference does not, by itself, establish that the warning prompted users to move their funds.

The discussion follows Zcash’s recent NU7 network upgrade, which improved transaction speed and continued the network’s transition away from older infrastructure.

Importantly, the immediate concern raised by Zakura is not evidence of a successful quantum attack. It relates to speculative advances in mathematics that could affect particular cryptographic constructions. Those advances remain unverified.

One of the problems its researchers are working on is the size of cryptographic proofs.

Stronger protection can require considerably more data to be processed and transmitted. That can create difficulties for blockchains, where transaction capacity, verification costs and storage requirements already matter.

The team is evaluating two possible approaches and expects to select a direction by the end of January 2027, provided its research progresses as planned.

Ironwood already incorporates features intended to support a future recovery mechanism. However, the developers have made clear that these features do not make Zcash fully quantum-resistant today.

The distinction is important. Having a contingency plan for a future attack is not the same as having protection against one.

Zcash is not the only network confronting these issues.

Bitcoin developers are discussing changes through proposals including BIP-360, which would introduce a transaction output format designed to reduce certain forms of public-key exposure.

A separate draft, BIP-361, explores a gradual transition away from vulnerable signature schemes once suitable alternatives are available.

Neither proposal should be confused with an activated Bitcoin upgrade.

Ethereum faces additional complications. Beyond individual wallets, its security model relies on cryptographic signatures used by validators and other infrastructure.

Ethereum’s quantum-security challenge extends to staking arrangements and institutional custody.

There is also a governance problem that applies particularly to Bitcoin. If millions of coins remain in old wallets that cannot be migrated, should the network eventually restrict their movement to prevent potential theft?

Doing so could protect the broader ecosystem, but it could also prevent legitimate owners from accessing their own money. Leaving those coins untouched carries a different set of risks.

Cryptography alone cannot settle that argument.

There is no reliable date for when a quantum computer capable of breaking widely used cryptocurrency signatures will become available.

Building such a machine requires more than increasing the number of qubits. Those qubits must also be reliable enough to carry out lengthy, complex calculations without errors overwhelming the results.

According to Coinbase Institute’s research, the relevant machines do not yet exist, but the process of upgrading blockchains, wallets and custody infrastructure could itself take years.

For that reason, waiting for an actual attack before implementing stronger cryptography would be a risky approach.

Crypto investors should pay attention to what developers implement, whether wallets support the new protections and whether existing funds can be migrated without compromising ownership.

There is no need to buy a token simply because its developers describe it as quantum-resistant, either. Such claims deserve scrutiny of the underlying cryptography and its implementation.

Zcash’s latest proposals offer a glimpse of the decisions other blockchain communities may eventually face. Replacing an algorithm is one thing. Persuading an entire decentralized financial network to move its money before a deadline is something else entirely.

In a recent turn of events, Fidelity Investments filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to launch a spot Chainlink [LINK] exchange-traded product (ETP).

According to the 25th November filing, the proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK. That said, the fund would also hold LINK tokens directly. This allows investors to gain exposure to LINK through traditional stock market accounts without having to purchase or manage the tokens themselves.

At the same time, the fund aims to track the Fidelity Chainlink Reference Rate, which calculates LINK’s price using a volume-weighted median methodology based on data from eligible spot markets.

Notably, its holdings would be managed by three proposed custodians, including Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust, and Coinbase Custody Trust Company.

As expected, this news did have a positive impact on LINK’s price, which was trading at $9.16 at press time after a hike of 5.5% in the past 24 hours. With this, Fidelity becomes the third asset manager to launch a LINK ETF besides Grayscale’s GLNK and Bitwise’s CLNK.

In fact, according to SoSo Value data, GLNK and CLNK have already recorded cumulative net inflows of $128.12 million and $47.88 million, respectively. This in turn has brought their combined cumulative inflows to approximately $176 million. However, neither fund recorded any new flows on the 25th of November, with both showing $0 in daily net inflows.

This news comes as the broader cryptocurrency investment products recorded widespread outflows across major digital assets in the month of November. Starting with Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs, which witnessed the largest withdrawals, worth approximately $5.39 billion in net outflows, facing their worst month since launch.

Ethereum [ETH] ETFs too saw $1.30 billion worth of outflows. This was followed by XRP ETFs, which saw $29.18 million in outflows, while Solana [SOL] ETFs registered withdrawals of $57 million. Meanwhile, Dogecoin [DOGE] ETFs recorded relatively smaller outflows of $409,130.

Interestingly, not all products experienced negative flows, as HBAR ETFs attracted approximately $1.71 million in net inflows. This made it the only asset in the sea of ETFs to record positive flows on the day.

Prices will need to hold above the $3.00–$3.10 area for support to begin to solidify buyers’ foothold above its long-term moving average.

From here, $3.20–$3.30 could act as resistance before the aforementioned moving averages (near $3.45–$3.75). For now, NEAR’s trend remains pressured though early signs of stabilization are starting to show after its extended drop from its October high near $5.90.

In the above chart, we can see that momentum has started to improve though the shorter- and medium-term moving averages still slope downwards and lie above prices.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) has started to improve after having approached oversold territory and though it has started to improve, it still sits below 50 which would indicate that prices still don’t show signs of momentum.

If sellers were to retake control and push prices back below $2.80, it could start to chip away at NEAR’s recovery and put its November low near $2.60 back into focus.

NEAR Protocol has announced that its House of Stake (HoS) has ratified HSP-029 which looks to reduce the maximum rate of token issuance in the NEAR network from 2.5% to 1.6% over the course of 24 months. The proposal, which passed with 99.96% of votes in favor and no veto from its Security Council, will see the issuance cap decrease in each epoch as the change goes into effect.

NEAR estimates that implementing HSP-029 would prevent the issuance of 11.8 million NEAR tokens over the next two years relative to keeping the 2.5% cap in place. The current breakdown of NEAR issuance (90% to staking participants and 10% to NEAR’s treasury) would remain unchanged.

As mentioned above, there is a grace period of one full quarter before HSP-029 can go into effect once ratified. For HSP-029 to go into effect, a network upgrade would need to be implemented and passed by validators.

Though it may provide NEAR token holders with some measure of protection from dilution in the long-run, it’s unlikely to cause any sort of immediate shift in demand given its implementation would also reduce gross staking rewards.

#5098. Binance Announces Dividends for Nvidia and Other Stocks

Binance will pay dividends to holders of stock tokens representing five companies: Nvidia, PayPal, Qualcomm, Western Digital, and Wendy’s.

The exchange will use the dividends paid by these companies to buy more stock tokens, allowing users to increase their holdings of the same stocks through the bStocks program.

The most important date for Nvidia token holders is Dec. 2. That's when Binance will take a snapshot of NVDAB balances at 01:00 UTC.

The snapshot for Wendy’s is scheduled for Dec. 1, followed by Nvidia on Dec. 2 and Qualcomm on Dec. 3.

Snapshots for PayPal and Western Digital are both scheduled for Dec. 4.

All snapshots will take place at 01:00 UTC.

In its Nov. 27 announcement, Binance provided the dates that will determine eligibility for dividends.

Binance plans to use Nvidia's cash dividends to purchase additional Nvidia shares, including fractional shares, after deducting applicable withholding taxes, fees, and other charges.

The proceeds will then be distributed among users who hold NVDAB on Binance and qualify for the dividend payment.

The same process will apply to the other four stocks.

If you hold eligible tokens in other products on the platform, such as savings or margin accounts, Binance will still credit the dividends to your spot account.

If you hold bStocks on-chain, the dividend payments will be made by adjusting the token's multiplier.

The tokens themselves are issued by Binance affiliate BTECH Holdings Limited, which owns the underlying securities.

So if you hold NVDAB, you have an interest in the Nvidia shares held by BTECH.

If you need to transfer tokens to Binance before the snapshot, you must do so at least two hours in advance.

Deposits and withdrawals of Nvidia tokens will be suspended at 23:00 UTC on Dec. 1.

The balance snapshot will take place at 01:00 UTC on Dec. 2.

Binance will also suspend one-to-one conversions between Nvidia shares and NVDAB tokens during this period.

The same two-hour suspension rule will apply to the other four stock tokens.

However, spot trading against USDT will continue, including trading in the NVDAB/USDT pair.

Binance said it would resume deposits, withdrawals and stock-to-token conversions after the dividend allocations are completed.

The exchange will not issue a separate announcement when these services resume.

#5097. New EU Crypto Sanctions Extend SWIFT’s Russia Blockade

Home » Blitz news » New EU Crypto Sanctions Extend SWIFT’s Russia Blockade

The Commission just granted a multi-faceted sanction package going ham on Russia’s various uses of crypto.

The European Commission’s 22nd sanctions package against Russia extends the European Union’s (EU) transaction ban to over 60 Russian banks and says all 60 of those will be removed from SWIFT, President Ursula von der Leyen said in Strasbourg on 23 November 2026.

This comes just weeks after Russia officially legalized crypto currency trading, starting with the big-cap coins like Bitcoin (BTC) & Ethereum (ETH). In the 22nd sanction packet, Russian-linked crypto services & platforms were specifically named as banned for transactions.

“The measures include the possibility for EU firms to sue their non-Russian contractual parties in the EU to recover damages.”, – states the document. “We will continue to propose new sanctions until Russia shows genuine intent for a lasting peace in Ukraine”, further said the Chief Commissioner.

With this package, we are increasing the pressure.We are striking harder at Russia’s ways to finance its war, by targeting its banks and crypto platforms.We are further isolating Russia. We are shutting the door to its participation to European sports and cultural events.… pic.twitter.com/9Ltkpohylq

While focusing on Russian SWIFT sanctions, the EU added 51 entities to the anti-circumvention list, while the majority of them, 27, were outside Russia: 14 came from China, including four in Hong Kong, four in Türkiye, three in Kyrgyzstan, two in India, two in Kazakhstan and two more in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

#5096. Bitcoin Whales Accumulate $7.4 Billion in BTC, Breaking a Nine Year Pattern

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Bitcoin whales have reversed their usual year-end pattern. Between September 30 and November 21, balances in addresses holding 1,000 to 10,000 BTC rose by 121,117 BTC even though Bitcoin lost 29.5% of its value. At a reference price of $61,000, those additional coins are worth roughly $7.4 billion.

The figures come from CryptoQuant’s November 27 research report, which was supported by crypto lender CoinRabbit. The study excludes exchange and mining-pool addresses from its balance cohorts. Its findings are a snapshot through November 21, not a final tally for the quarter.

The timing matters. NewsBTC recently reported more than $2 billion in US spot Bitcoin ETF outflows. Fund withdrawals and rising whale balances point in different directions, but they measure different things. Neither tells us whether the same investors are moving their money from ETFs into direct Bitcoin ownership.

A broader measure from Maketo’s whale holdings data puts the balance of addresses with at least 1,000 BTC at 7.22 million BTC on November 26, up 54,379 BTC over the preceding 30 days. That group includes exchange and custody addresses, so it provides a separate view of where coins are held rather than an independent check of CryptoQuant’s 121,117 BTC figure.

The combined balance of the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort at just under 2.95 million BTC on November 21, up from 2.83 million at the end of September.

Large addresses reduced their balances in seven of the nine preceding fourth quarters. Only 2019 and 2020 escaped that pattern. The 4.29% increase recorded so far this quarter is the largest Q4 gain since 2020, although December could still change the result.

For comparison, the cohort lost nearly 203,000 BTC over Q4 2025. This year’s increase has come during a falling market, rather than a rally.

There is a catch in calling this a $7.4 billion accumulation. The figure values the additional coins at a reference price; it does not measure the dollars spent buying them. Transfers between addresses, including movements across the cohort’s balance thresholds, can change the total without a market purchase.

The increase tells us where Bitcoin is sitting. It does not tell us how much fresh capital is behind it. That distinction matters when liquidity is scarce.

The 121,117 BTC figure makes for a bullish headline. The number I would pay closer attention to is the remaining profit margin.

Among addresses holding between 1,000 and 10,000 BTC, the unrealized profit margin fell from 33.9% at the end of September to 5.7% on November 21, its lowest reading of 2026 in the report.

The deterioration is even clearer in dollar terms. Combined unrealized profits for addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC stood at about $24 billion on November 21, down from a peak of $294 billion in August 2025.

Across the broader group of addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC, net realized losses reached approximately $2.1 billion in the first 52 days of Q4. The on-chain data suggests that some large holders are already moving coins at a loss rather than waiting for a recovery.

The relevant distinction is between the balance held at a given date and the profit or loss on coins that move. A growing balance does not prevent other coins within the cohort from being spent below their estimated cost basis.

Exchange deposits deserve a closer look, too. Inflows from unspent transaction outputs (UTXOs) of at least 1,000 BTC averaged 5,012 BTC per day in November through the report’s cutoff, compared with 3,239 in October. That is a measure of large coin outputs, not a count of individual whales.

November’s pickup should not obscure the bigger picture: the quarter-to-date average of 3,955 BTC per day remained below the 2019–2025 Q4 average of 4,575 BTC. Large deposits are not proof of sales, and a rise in this metric alone does not establish that selling pressure has intensified.

The 2018 and 2022 bear markets offer a useful comparison, though not a roadmap for this one.

Balances in the 1,000 to 10,000 BTC cohort declined in both of those fourth quarters. Their average unrealized profit margins were negative, while the group still had a positive margin at the November 21 reading this year.

Today’s accumulation may be a sign that some large holders are willing to retain exposure through the downturn. The address data cannot establish their motives or identify how much of the increase came from new purchases.

I would not call a market bottom on these numbers alone.

A further price decline could wipe out the cohort’s remaining profit cushion. Whether that produces more selling depends on the holders’ liquidity needs and positioning, neither of which can be read directly from address balances.

The next test is whether large-address balances keep rising while net realized losses and large exchange deposits ease. That combination, alongside evidence of renewed spot demand, would make the recovery case more convincing.

For now, the change in year-end positioning is real within CryptoQuant’s measured cohort. Evidence of a durable recovery is still missing.

#5095. Bank of Japan Warns Stablecoins and Tokenization Threaten Financial Stability

Japan's central bank has warned that automated trading in tokenized markets could exacerbate a sell-off.

It also raised concerns about whether stablecoin holders can always redeem their tokens at face value.

A Bank of Japan executive director outlined these risks during his keynote speech at an International Monetary Fund seminar in Tokyo.

In the event of a price drop, according to Kazushige Kamiyama, a smart contract could automatically increase the amount of collateral required. It could also trigger a sale of the collateral backing a position if the borrower doesn't have enough collateral.

These sales could drive prices even lower, potentially spreading financial stress across institutions and markets.

In the case of stablecoins, the question is whether a token with a face value of one dollar can always be redeemed for one dollar.

To ensure this, issuers' reserves need to be properly regulated, and the links to central bank money need to be reliable, Kamiyama said.

A bank might have enough cash to pay for a trade in tokenized assets but still be unable to complete the payment.

This could happen when a trade is settled overnight, and the payment system the bank uses to transfer cash is unavailable.

The bank might have to keep additional cash on a trading platform. Meanwhile, cash held on another network might not be accessible when the payment is due.

"Even with faster settlement, it does not necessarily lead to efficient liquidity management," Kamiyama said.

Cross-border securities trades, however, could benefit from tokenization.

A smart contract could link the payment and delivery of a security so that both transactions are executed simultaneously.

This could reduce the risk of a buyer paying for an asset without receiving it.

The Bank of Japan is setting up a testing environment with financial institutions that hold accounts at the central bank.

One scenario involves exploring how cash settlement could work for trades involving tokenized Japanese government bonds.

The central bank is considering two options for making the cash payment.

One would involve issuing tokenized central bank money. The other would link a token trading platform to Japan's existing payment infrastructure.

These tests will evaluate whether the proposed solutions can address the challenges financial institutions face when settling trades.

#5093. Why Sleep Consistency May Be the Missing Piece When It Comes to Heart Health

It’s not just about getting 7 to 9 hours anymore.

You probably already know that getting seven to nine hours of sleep each night is one of the best things you can do for your health and wellbeing. But what happens if you’re consistently hitting that goal while going to bed at different times? Think 10 p.m. on Monday, midnight on Wednesday, and well past 1 a.m. on Saturday because it’s the weekend, after all.

As it turns out, your heart might not be too happy about that. New research suggests that sleep consistency—which includes both when you go to bed and wake up, and how much sleep you get from night to night—could play an important role in cardiovascular health. And, while getting the recommended amount of shut-eye still matters, researchers are finding that how much your sleep fluctuates may deserve some attention, too.

Before you start stressing over every late night or weekend sleep-in, though, there's some important context to understand. Here's what the research actually found, why your body seems to care so much about routine, and how consistent your sleep schedule really needs to be.

Meet the experts: Nguyen Minh Tuan Viet, MD, PhD, is a neuroscientist and postdoctoral research fellow at Boston Children's Hospital and Harvard Medical School and lead researcher of the new study. Nour Makarem, PhD, is a cardiovascular epidemiologist in the department of epidemiology at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health. Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, is a professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center.

For the new study published in Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, researchers analyzed more than one million nights of sleep data from 10,362 adults participating in the National Institutes of Health's All of Us Research Program, an initiative that aims to collect data from over one million Americans and create the country’s largest biomedical database.

Unlike previous studies that only looked at people's sleep habits for about a week, this one used about six months of Fitbit data to see how participants' bedtimes, wake-up times, and total sleep duration changed from night to night. They then compared those patterns with participants’ medical records and tracked their health for nearly four years.

The findings were pretty eye-opening: For every additional 29 minutes of variation in how long someone slept from night to night, their relative risk of serious heart problems, including heart attacks, heart failure, heart muscle disease, and certain strokes, was 24 percent higher. To be clear, that doesn't mean going to bed 29 minutes later than usual on a given night increases your heart disease risk by 24 percent. The researchers were looking at a statistical measure of how much someone's total sleep duration varied over time, rather than the consequences of one late bedtime. As of now, all this information does it point to a potential link between sleep schedule variation and heart disease.

Researchers also found that greater night-to-night fluctuations in bedtime and wake-up times were associated with a 23 percent and 20 percent higher relative risk of cardiovascular problems, respectively. This means that both the consistency of your sleep schedule and the consistency of the duration of that sleep may play a role in heart health.

There are a few things worth keeping in mind, though. For starters, this study found a connection between inconsistent sleep and heart problems, but it couldn't prove that irregular sleep is what causes those problems. In fact, Viet points out that the relationship could work in the opposite direction too (i.e. early illness might actually make someone’s sleep more irregular). Plus, most participants were women and white, so we can't necessarily assume the findings apply to everyone. Still, the results add to growing evidence that sleep consistency deserves a place in the heart-health conversation.

Your body has its own internal clock, known as your circadian rhythm, which determines when you're tired, when you're wide awake, and even how bodily functions like blood pressure and heart rate change throughout the day. And, it works at its best when it has a reasonably predictable schedule to follow. When you're constantly changing when you sleep and wake, you may disrupt that rhythm, a phenomenon known as circadian misalignment, explains Nour Makarem, PhD, a cardiovascular epidemiologist in the department of epidemiology at Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health.

That disruption can impact some pretty important cardiovascular processes, like how your body regulates blood pressure. Under normal circumstances, blood pressure usually drops by about 10 to 20 percent while you're sleeping to give your cardiovascular system a period of rest, but research by Makarem suggests that irregular sleep patterns may be associated with higher blood pressure and an increased risk of hypertension. “This is problematic because higher nocturnal blood pressure and having a non-dipping profile (blood pressure that does not dip or dip enough during sleep) are associated with higher risk for heart disease and stroke, the leading causes of death in women,” she says.

Your sleep schedule may also interact with other daily rhythms, including when you eat and exercise. These behaviors help regulate biological clocks throughout your body, including those involved in metabolism, Makarem says. When those clocks fall out of sync, processes like blood sugar regulation may be affected, too. In fact, research has linked irregular sleep patterns with poorer glucose regulation and a higher risk of metabolic issues.

Research is still emerging, but scientists are noticing some important links between sleep consistency and heart health. A 2025 study published in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health followed more than 72,000 adults and found that people with irregular sleep patterns had a higher risk of major cardiovascular events, including heart attacks and strokes. Another study published in Sleep in 2024 analyzed sleep patterns in more than 60,000 adults and found that sleep regularity was a stronger predictor of mortality risk than sleep duration in that population.

So, does this mean having a consistent bed and rising time matters more than getting eight hours? Not necessarily. "The evidence for sleep regularity is rather nascent relative to that for sleep duration," says Marie-Pierre St-Onge, PhD, a professor of nutritional medicine and director of the Center of Excellence for Sleep & Circadian Research at Columbia University Irving Medical Center. She explains that while several studies have made the connection between irregular sleep and poorer health outcomes, more research needs to be done to determine whether making someone's sleep schedule more consistent can actually lower their cardiovascular risk. And, we do have plenty of evidence that getting enough sleep has positive affects on just about every system in the body, from brain function to muscle recovery.

Overall, there are still things researchers are learning about sleep consistency and heart health, but it’s safe to start thinking of it as another piece of the puzzle, alongside getting enough hours and making sure those hours are restorative.

Here's the million-dollar question: Does protecting your heart mean going to bed at exactly 10:30 p.m. every single night, no exceptions? Thankfully, no.

Ultimately, you’ve got some wiggle room. "In general, we would recommend that individuals try not to deviate by 60 min up or down from their average bedtime or sleep duration," says St-Onge, but the smaller the gap, the better.

Think of that as a target, not a hard-and-fast rule. An occasional late night or weekend sleep-in isn’t a reason to panic. What matters more is establishing a reasonably consistent pattern over a period of time rather than expecting yourself to follow a perfect schedule every single night.

If you've had a particularly short night, St-Onge recommends trying to go to bed a little earlier and waking up a little later when your schedule allows, rather than trying to make up for all that lost sleep by sleeping in for hours. Most importantly, don't sweat it. "If one night is off, it's not all doom and gloom; you get right back on schedule the following night," says St-Onge.

Here are a few small changes experts recommend to improve your sleep routine without completely overhauling your lifestyle.

Before committing to being in bed every night by 9 p.m., consider what will actually make sense for your schedule. Earlier isn't automatically better. What's important is getting adequate sleep on a schedule that works with your body's natural rhythm and everyday responsibilities, explains St-Onge.

If your current bedtime is midnight but you'd ideally like to be asleep by 11, there's no need to make that change all at once. Makarem recommends gradually shifting your bedtime earlier by about 10 minutes each day until you reach your target. The idea is to give your body time to adjust rather than suddenly expecting yourself to fall asleep an hour earlier than usual.

It's tempting to stay up late on Friday and Saturday nights and make up for it by sleeping well into the morning, but even those brief changes can leave you feeling out of sync by the time Monday rolls around. If possible, St-Onge recommends keeping your weekend bedtimes within about an hour of your usual routine.

If you wear an Apple Watch or Fitbit to bed, you know how easy it is to get caught up in the numbers. One morning you're celebrating a great sleep score, and the next you're wondering what went wrong because your tracker says you barely got any deep sleep.

While these devices can be helpful for spotting patterns, the last thing you want is to start losing sleep over your sleep. Makarem recommends using trackers to keep tabs on your habits or remind you when it's time for bed, but only if they're actually helping. If checking your sleep stats is making you anxious, it's fine to ditch the data and simply pay attention to when you're going to bed and waking up.

And remember, you don't have to get your sleep schedule exactly right every single night to do something good for your heart. Small changes that you can actually stick with are worth more than chasing a perfect score. As Makarem puts it, "Progress is better than perfect."

Monero (XMR) is not welcome on top exchanges as the series of delistings takes an uglier turn for holders following Kucoin's XMR removal. But Kucoin wasn't first and might not be the last: XMR was removed from MEXC, Kraken, Binance and others already.

The main issue for an asset that's being removed from exchanges will always be the liquidity. In the last 24 hours, Monero's spot flow lost $1.3 million. Despite the increasing volume, the asset is recording outflows and exchange withdrawals. The volume spike is most like being a reflection of a substantial selling activity.

In a single day, XMR was losing almost 20% of its value. If it wasn't for the delisting, price could've broken multiple technical resistances already and confirmed a recovery. As of November 27, the price is slowly recovering, following the general relief on the cryptocurrency market.

On November 26, Kucoin announced the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC trading pairs, effective November 30. The exchange has already limited any deposits, with withdrawals available for all users.

Monero is an inherently private cryptocurrency, that limits the ability of explorers to determine transaction destination and senders. That is the main reason centralized exchanges are removing XMR.

For holders, the problem is not that Monero stops working after a delisting. The network is still active, and XMR can be transferred between wallets or traded on exchanges that continue to support it. The problem is that there are fewer places to buy and sell it. If more large exchanges follow Kucoin, liquidity could become lower, making new selling activity more painful for the price.

#5090. Why XRP Analysts Flag $8.30 Macro Price Target

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Why XRP Analysts Flag $8.30 Macro Price Target

The wild SWIFT replacement claim resurfaces on social media for a good reason: XRP-tied banks are in.

Two recent posts have put long-term XRP price projections back in view. One centers on a multi-year chart pattern with an $8.30 target, while the other argues that full replacement of SWIFT would support valuations above $15,000. XRP is trading near $0.95.

Analyst EGRAG CRYPTO highlighted a weekly chart showing a large symmetrical triangle that XRP broke out of in prior years. The X post stated that the original white triangle’s measured breakout target of $8.30 has not yet been reached and suggested the current price action could represent a macro retest of that breakout before any larger expansion.

#XRP – The $8.30 Number 🎯:This remains one of my most powerful macro charts.The original white symmetrical triangle breakout target has STILL not been reached.What if everything happening right now is simply the macro retest of that breakout before the real expansion?My… pic.twitter.com/F0tdM5mxtl

The chart marks $1.65 as a major reclaim and confirmation level, with $8.30 labeled as the primary macro target. EGRAG noted a personal connection to the number.

Being born in 1983, and said that level is where a large portion of holdings would be sold if reached. The analysis frames the target as a technical outcome rather than an emotional one. XRP remains well below its 2025 high near $3.65, and the pattern’s interpretation is subject to debate among traders.

A separate post by Ripple_Mino claimed that if XRP fully replaces SWIFT, the token could be valued beyond $15,000. The argument rests on XRP’s divisibility: one XRP equals one million drops, so even extreme valuations would still allow practical fractional use.

When XRP replaces Swift, it will be valued beyond $15,000 per token.The original token design allowed for such a valuation as 1 XRP can be divided into 1,000,000 smaller units known as drops.So 1 Drop = 0.000001 XRP(one millionth of an XRP) pic.twitter.com/WcBEPSh0XA

Official and recent developments do not support the premise of XRP’s SWIFT replacement.

SWIFT has launched its own blockchain-based shared ledger for tokenized bank deposits, with more than a dozen major banks participating in trials. SWIFT has not announced any integration of XRP as a settlement asset for that system.

Former SWIFT innovation leadership has publicly rejected claims of XRP integration, and the network continues to emphasize its own infrastructure and tokenized deposits rather than a single external token.

The $8.30 figure is a technical target drawn from a multi-year chart structure, while the $15,000 figure is a hypothetical based on a scenario that SWIFT and major participating banks haven’t endorsed yet.

Neither projection is reflected in current market pricing yet or officially top-confirmed institutional commitments. XRP’s price action continues to trade well below both levels as of late November 2026.

The link between SWIFT as a traditional financial intermediary and XRP’s native chain comes multi-layered, with intersection across liquidity provision and instant settlement environments.

Stablecoin giant Tether [USDT] has been making some moves lately. Here’s the rundown.

Tether has backed Argentine fintech app Lemon, with the former not putting a number on it when it announced the deal. Lemon did, however, saying that the package is worth $14.5 million.

According to Lemon CEO Marcelo Cavazzoli, only $5 million of that is an actual investment in the company’s shares. The other $9.5 million is an incentive plan linked to products the two will build together.

There’s a lot that’s unclear right now though. Neither side has shared Lemon’s valuation or how big a stake Tether is getting. There’s also no word on how or when the $9.5 million gets paid out. Tether is after more users for USDT and Tether Gold [XAUT] across Latin America. Lemon gives it a decent shot at that. The app is said to have 4.5 million verified users, and its main balance runs on USDT.

Worth noting, however, that Lemon’s not the only home for Tether this month.

On the 9th, D3 launched a USD vault for Tether’s stablecoin. Users can deposit USDT, keep an eye on their position, and withdraw without leaving the platform.

Sentora built the system using its Earn OS and Upshift tools, which decide where deposited funds go. Money moves with the market, within a set of risk rules. It is said that the setup has already handled more than $2 billion.

Domain buyers usually come in, make a deal, and leave. Earning on stablecoins gives them a reason to keep their money on the platform.

Just don’t mistake automated for guaranteed. Returns depend on the lending markets the vault uses. So, users are still trusting a whole stack of infrastructure with their dollars.

#5088. Ripple's David Schwartz Shuts Down XRP Escrow Burn Idea: Even 80% Can’t Force It

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz said on Friday that XRP Ledger validators cannot force the rest of the network to burn Ripple's escrowed XRP, even with more than 80% support. According to Schwartz, the XRP Ledger has "no coercive mechanism at all."

Schwartz, one of the creators of the XRP Ledger, made the comments in two replies on X on Thursday and Friday. The thread started on Wednesday with a post from an XRP community member. According to the post, "validators have no say over Ripple's escrow," and Ripple runs one validator on the default Unique Node List (dUNL), not three.

Another X user then asked: "Couldn't validators pass an amendment that would burn Ripple's escrow? Changes to the code of the XRPL could do anything..." Schwartz answered on Thursday that such validators would "just disagree with everyone else who didn't want that change and be counted as disagreeing validators, effectively isolating themselves from the network."

If the majority of nodes want something, nothing can stop them from having it. They just can't force those who don't agree to go along with them. But the same is true for a minority of nodes too. There's no coercive mechanism at all.

On Friday, the same user asked whether the answer would change if "the vast majority (80+%)" wanted the burn. "If the majority of nodes want something, nothing can stop them from having it. They just can't force those who don't agree to go along with them. But the same is true for a minority of nodes too. There's no coercive mechanism at all," Schwartz wrote.

On Nov. 16, a group of XRP holders called Make XRP Great Again demanded in an open letter to Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse that the company burn 31.1 billion escrowed XRP by March 31, 2027. XRP Insights recorded the same amount in 99 escrow objects that day. Ripple reported 31.7 billion XRP in escrow as of Sept. 30.

According to XRPScan, an amendment on the XRP Ledger needs 29 of 35 validator votes, or more than 80%, and has to keep that support for two weeks before it activates.

In late 2020, Schwartz wrote on X that "if the majority wants a rules change, there is nothing the minority can do to stop them." On Feb. 19, 2024, he wrote that Ripple "could unilaterally create the same effect as burning an escrow by provably blackholing the account the escrow completes into."

In February 2026, Schwartz argued with Cyber Capital founder Justin Bons on X. Bons called the XRP Ledger centralized and said that its Unique Node List gives Ripple control over consensus. Schwartz described the claims as "objectively nonsensical."

Ripple's next monthly escrow release of 1 billion XRP is scheduled for Dec. 1. In its Nov. 16 letter, Make XRP Great Again also asked Garlinghouse for a public response and a verifiable plan for the burn.

#5087. The Most Comfortable Sneakers for Women, Tested by a Style Writer

We’ve put hundreds of sneakers to the test, and On is at the top of my list.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

At this point, I’m pretty sure I qualify as the woman who lived in her shoes. Not in a glamorous Carrie Bradshaw kind of way, but in a professional-sneaker-tester kind of way. I probs have at least 30 pairs crowding my closet and entryways right now, and that’s not even counting the pairs I’ve run into the ground or given away to friends and family (you’re welcome). My top priority is always comfort, and while you might find that a given when it comes to sneakers, I’ve tested my fair share of options that make my feet feel stiff and achy.

So, I present to you the pairs of comfortable shoes—think walking shoes and cross-training shoes—that actually keep me feeling comfortable and supported without slacking on cuteness. From memory foam insoles that mold to your foot's unique shape to running shoes with responsive soles that absorb your stride’s shock, these are the most comfortable sneakers for women, tested by myself and other sneaker enthusiasts at Women’s Health.

The brand ethos of On is to make people feel like they're running on Clouds. It achieves this thanks to its signature Helion Superfoam midsole, which sets itself apart with a construction that blends rigid, stable sections with flexible foam. This combination of materials provides the perfect balance of cushioning and energy return, giving you a bouncy, lightweight feel when your foot hits the pavement. The result is a soft, natural ground feel, rather than an overly bouncy cushioning experience. Fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi says this tech alone is why this shoe is an absolute workhorse when it comes to running (and running fast!). It’s her all-time favorite race shoe—she even ran a half-marathon in it.

According to Accardi, the shoe feels firm but still has enough flexibility that her running gait isn’t impacted. The toebox has a ton of room for movement, but still holds the foot in place so each step feels responsive and energetic. Even when her legs feel like they’re about to give out, these shoes pick her right back up. On’s innovative speedboard, a flexible plastic plate wedged between the footbed and midsole, snaps back into place for a bouncy effect after your feet hit the ground. This means the shoe requires less energy output with each stride, making running feel easier. Plus, the rebound that comes with the underfoot cushioning gives a spring in your step.

I might not run marathons like Accardi, but I love to wear this shoe for walking and casual jogs. The CloudTec system, which uses air pockets in the midsole (the layer between the insole and the outsole), to create the shoe’s cushiony feel, propels me forward with every step, kind of like walking on a trampoline. And while it’s great for getting your steps in, this shoe has that chunky look that’s super on trend right now. I love pairing it with tailored pants and a boxy T-shirt on top for that upgraded activewear vibe.

One thing to note, though, is the sole wears down fast, which we found to be disappointing, especially given that price tag. Accardi says the Clifton 10 has a better tread thanks to its thicker outsole designed for high-friction.

Out of all the sneakers I’ve tried, I find myself wearing the Brooks Ghost Max 3—it’s the newest addition to the Ghost Max series—the most when I want to feel comfortable during walks or runs (yep, it can do both!). That’s because the rocker bottom sole, which has a slight curve to it like a rocking chair, helps propel my foot forward with less energy. Wearing it literally feels like walking on pillows.

With the most cushioning of any shoe on this list (and the most cushioning Brooks offers), it’s perfect for those who need extra support. Fitness contributor Talene Appleton says it has extra plush, foamy cushioning, but even for a max cushioned shoe, it’s incredibly stable thanks to Brooks’ signature Guardrails technology, which is a broad base with two pieces of foam on either side of the heel. It reduces the rolling of the foot both inward and outward, so it cradles your foot in place without messing with your stride. According to Appleton, this combination is great for those with higher arches. After hours of walking, she doesn’t feel an ounce of pain or discomfort. And if you have wide feet or bunions, you’re in luck—this shoe comes in both wide and extra-wide options (huge win!).

During testing, I did notice that there was some wear and tear on the shoe pretty early on (it had only been a few months of use). The material on the upper of the shoe wore out pretty quickly. While this knocked it down a few points in my book, its supreme comfort still kept this kick at the very top of my list. Plus, I love how many fun colors the shoe comes in—because running and walking should be fun, right?!

The Hoka Clifton 11 is a standout favorite among WH editors. After testing nearly every Hoka model, I can attest that the Clifton 11 reigns supreme for walking. I was also a fan of the previous Clifton 10, and the newest version feels very similar—just a smidge lighter and more springy. It is by far the most comfortable model in the series to date, and it’s earned a spot in my shoe rotation for its supportive yet flexible cushioning.

The first major difference I noticed is how light the Clifton 11 feels. Even after wearing it for several hours at a time, it doesn’t feel bulky or clunky. Which makes sense: Hoka did shave nearly half an ounce off the weight compared to the 10. The toe box is slightly narrower, too, but it doesn’t feel tight or uncomfortable. I prefer the more secure fit because it kept my foot from sliding around without feeling cramped. If you like a little more wiggle room for your toes, I would suggest opting for the wide sizing, though.

Despite its lighter weight, it has a generous stack of foam padding throughout the midsole. That weightless yet cushiony feel makes it ideal for my longer walks throughout NYC. The shoe has a mild heel drop (the same as the previous model at 8 mm), which helps distribute pressure evenly across the foot.

I also find that the foam absorbs impact well. My feet—unfortunately plagued by plantar fasciitis—never feel fatigued wearing this shoe. There's technically a rocker shape built into the sole, but it's subtle enough that I barely notice it—instead, my stride feels smooth and natural whether I’m walking or running. I’m also a fan of the durable rubber outsole that gives plenty of traction. I never feel like I’m going to slip while wearing these, even when walking down slippery subway stairs.

So far, the Clifton 11—which was debuted alongside the new Clifton Pro— does a great job of keeping my feet comfy and supported. It’s a great shoe for anyone in need of a comfortable, everyday walking sneaker that can also handle the occasional jog (unlike the Clifton Pro, which is geared more toward high-speed running).

Read more: Hoka Clifton 11 and Clifton Pro Review

There’s nothing worse than slipping into an uncomfortable shoe after a tough run—that’s where the Alo Recovery Sneaker comes in. Designed to support tired feet, it features a structured sole and high-rebound foam insole that offers arch support and bounces back into place with each step. It makes every step feel stable, cushioned, and balanced. The second I put this pair on after a long run, my feet are instantly relaxed. I can’t say that about most of my other sneakers.

One of the biggest perks of this shoe? The traction is next-level, which is key for a recovery sneaker that’s meant to keep you comfortable and steady all day. Inside, the sock-like lining prevents your foot from sliding around. The thick ankle collar also helps stabilize the foot and provides extra support up the leg, keeping everything locked in place.

Style-wise, this sneaker goes with everything—sweats, shorts, jeans, leggings, you name it. That’s why I crowned it the best overall platform sneaker. After giving it a spin for a few weeks running around Manhattan, walking my dog around Long Island, and wearing it to and from workout classes, it's done the best job at keeping my feet pain-free compared to many other platform sneakers I've worn. The 1.5-inch platform is subtle but adds just the right amount of height to elongate my legs without being so tall that I feel unstable. Oh, and it’s super cute to boot. I’m a big fan of the Natural White colorway, which looks clean and classic, and pairs effortlessly with everything from sweatpants to denim.

Even if you’re not fresh off a run, it works for the office, errands, or a casual lunch. It’s hands down one of the most versatile (and most worn) shoes in my closet. My one con is that it feels a bit heavy and bulky, especially after a long day of wear.

Read more: Alo Recovery Mode Sneaker Review

I hadn't tried Asics until this year, and now it's my go-to shoe brand. Not only does its shoe have a streetwear vibe (I'm loving the bright yellow color with sweats and jeans), but they’re also some of the most comfortable shoes I’ve ever worn. In the UB9-S Gel Kayano 20s, the brand uses its signature gel cushioning technology, which features gel units placed in both the heel and forefoot of the shoe to absorb shock and provide a soft landing. This cushioning adapts to your foot’s movement, offering flexibility while reducing impact on your joints. Plus, the form-fitting upper keeps your foot locked in place, making it perfect for long runs, but stylish enough for everyday wear.

I wear this shoe everywhere—on runs, in the gym, and even to the office—and I get compliments virtually every single time I step out in it. The support is unmatched, the traction is solid, and it’s lightweight enough that I never feel weighed down. Plus, it breaks in fast (I wore it right out of the box), so there’s no awkward adjustment period. If you’re looking for a sneaker that can do it all while still looking cool, this is the one for you.

One con to note: It comes in some funky colors, so if you’re not into something bright and fun, I’d recommend looking elsewhere. I also wish it came in a wider version for those with wider feet and bunions.

We’ve been fans of the Chargefeel line for years, with the previous edition—the Chargefeel 2—winning the best cross-training shoe for our 2025 WH Sneaker Awards. Lululemon has since made a few tweaks that make it even better. “Everyone I know who has worked out in the Chargefeel—myself included—has loved its perfect balance of stability and flexibility,” says WH executive health and fitness director Jacqueline Andriakos, NASM-CPT.

Now with a lighter weight and a lower heel-to-toe drop (6 mm compared to 9.5 mm), the shoe doesn’t weigh me down and puts less stress on the ankles and feet. I’m a big fan of the wider base for lifting and squatting because it makes my feet feel locked. The forefoot-hugging band on the inside of the shoe and a tough plastic heel counter add extra security, while the springy EVA foam cushioning makes it a workhorse for walking and running.

And post-workout, it’s a great leisure kick for traveling or running errands. I recently wore this sneaker while traveling, and it kept my feet happy power walking through the airport and standing in long security and customs lines. Andriakos agrees, stating, “The stylish silhouette looks good outside the gym.”

The fit is true to size, and while wide-size options are not available, the toes still have adequate room to spread with each step or lift. However, the wide outsole may feel too bulky during stair climbing or quick, dynamic moves.

Let me introduce you to my new favorite low-profile, fashion sneaker: the Puma Speedcat. It’s been making waves with style girls, and after testing it out for months, I can see why. This shoe pairs so well with any outfit, with a slim, almost ballet-flat silhouette that doesn’t clash with nicer pieces in my wardrobe. I even see celebs like Em Rata sport the Speedcat all the time, and they always make any streetwear ‘fit look so chic and cool.

Like the Samba, it has a pretty flat sole, but I actually find it more cushioned thanks to its EVA midsole, which has a lightweight, cushioned feel and shock-absorbing properties. This means I can walk around for longer without my feet aching. Plus, after wearing it on wet city streets, I’ve noticed it has better traction, which is a huge win.

The only downside? The fit is a little narrow, especially in the toe area. If you have wider feet, I’d definitely recommend sizing up.

Originally designed for indoor soccer, the Adidas Samba has become a cult-favorite sneaker that’s just as popular on the streets as it is on the field. At first glance, the Samba looks pretty flat, so I wasn’t expecting much in terms of comfort. But after logging hundreds of miles walking around the city, I was surprised by how well it supports my feet. The Samba uses a combination of synthetic leather for the upper and a rubber sole with a cushioned midsole for comfort. The cushioning is more subtle compared to high-performance running shoes, but it still provides a soft, supportive feel. Even without a ton of cushioning, I rarely experience discomfort, which is impressive for a sneaker this sleek. It runs narrow, especially for wide feet, and I recommend going a half size down, as it tends to run big—many with wider feet or bunions agree it’s not the best fit.

It’s a go-to for effortlessly cool outfits—you can wear it with jeans, dresses, slacks, or shorts and always look stylish. I own this shoe in two different colorways (it comes in so many different shades), and after wearing it with practically everything in my closet, I can confidently say it adds a sporty, trendy touch to any outfit.

One of Under Armour’s first-ever shoes, this kick is rooted in sport. But it’s gotten some essential upgrades since its launch, and it’s safe to say I’m hooked. Since 2009, it’s been updated with leather upper overlays to keep the foot supported and soft UA HOVR cushioning, made from soft EVA foam and rubber, which is engineered to store and release energy with each step, providing a bouncy, responsive feel that helps propel you forward. Out of all the shoes I’ve tried, this pair feels the most bouncy, which I know is an absolute essential for the runners and walkers out there that like that super thick underfoot feel. It also has a rocker shape to keep the foot in a forward motion for less energy exertion.

The UA Apparition also has a mesh upper for supreme breathability—I’ve worn it during HIIT workouts, runs, and walks and never feel like my feet are constricted or sweaty, but I still feel supported and balanced. With a sleek, minimalistic look, the Apparition pairs well with anything from gym gear to casual streetwear. The rubber outsole provides traction and durability, allowing for smooth transitions during both dynamic workouts and everyday use.

My one con? There are some fun colors available, but I wish there were more options to choose from.

When it comes to comfortable sneakers, cushioning should be your top priority—whether you’re walking, running, hitting the gym, or just running errands. Here are the cushioning levels you can expect to see in the shoes below:

As Women’s Health editors, we practically live in sneakers, so we know what it takes for a shoe to feel super comfortable. When I originally put together this list of the most comfortable sneakers in 2025, I spent over two years testing more than 50 pairs in every possible scenario—long and short walks, runs, HIIT workouts, full days out in NYC, travel days, and more. For this 2026 update, myself and other WH editors re-tested newer iterations of our favorite pairs to make sure they still meet our standards. I also sought advice from fitness contributors Nicolette Accardi and Talene Appleton, as well as style contributor Lily Wohlner. We looked at everything from cushioning and stability to sizing, traction, and color options. And if a pair left our feet aching or uncomfortable, it didn’t make the cut. So you can trust that every sneaker on this list kept our feet happy all day long—even through our toughest workouts.

NEAR Protocol’s [NEAR] token rallied by 7.4% in the last 24 hours, making it one of the biggest winners among the top-20 crypto assets by market capitalization. The altcoin’s daily trading volume hiked by nearly 45% too.

As with most other altcoins, the question with NEAR is — Can the buyers convert the short-term momentum into something lasting? Or will the uncertainty around Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] snuff out any bullish hopes for NEAR?

From August to October, NEAR rallied by 290%, from $1.53 to $6. Surging cross-chain swap volume on NEAR Intents, a cut in the maximum annual token issuance from 2.6% to 1.5%, and the confidential perpetual futures roll-out helped boost bullish sentiment.

The subsequent price rally was met with short liquidations, driving further gains.

After hitting its $6-high, the altcoin underwent a 50% correction and sunk to $3 once again.

The 3-day timeframe’s price structure was bullish at press time. The altcoin’s price approached the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level at $2.49, climbing to $3.04 at the time of writing.

Now, although the RSI was below neutral-50, the OBV has held up well in recent weeks’ selling. This may be a sign that after the 50% correction, buyers might be able to push the trend back in their favor.

On the contrary, the 4-hour price structure was bearish. A trading session close above $3.28 is needed to flip the internal structure bullishly. A sustained move above $3.47 is required to confirm this timeframe’s bullish swing structure shift.

And yet, the first bullish sign has already occurred. The imbalance (white box) at $2.75 has been respected on the charts, kickstarting the gains made in the last 24 hours.

Given that this is a good start, bulls can keep an eye on NEAR token‘s progress. $3.47 will be the pivotal level that would signal a credible bullish trend shift.

#5085. Bitcoin miners are shutting down machines, but mining just got even harder

Bitcoin's mining difficulty jumped 7.61% despite the network recording its first annual hashrate contraction since China's 2021 mining ban.

Bitcoin's mining difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov. 27, intensifying financial pressure on miners already switching off machines.

Data from Mempool.space showed that the adjustment took effect at 05:17 UTC at block 977,760, raising mining difficulty from 134.82 trillion to 145.09 trillion.

Since expected mining rewards per unit of computing power move inversely to difficulty, the increase reduces what Bitcoin miners can expect to earn from their existing machines by 7.08%, assuming average transaction fees remain unchanged.

From a starting price of $60,000, Bitcoin would need to climb approximately 7.61% to $64,570 for miners to restore their previous gross dollar revenue.

Bitcoin mining difficulty rose 7.61% on Nov. 27. The chart holds hashrate and block rewards fixed.

At unchanged fees, the modeled price rise of about 7.61% would restore expected gross mining revenue to its pre-reset level.

Illustrative expected gross revenue per unit of hashrate. The comparison holds subsidy and average fees in BTC per block fixed. Actual payouts and operating costs vary.

Divide old difficulty (134,823,837,323,273) by new difficulty (145,088,938,867,954) for a revenue index of 92.924959 at unchanged price, with average fees and subsidy fixed. Reverse that ratio for the price multiplier (1.076137). Graphic labels are rounded.

Illustrative expected gross revenue per unit of hashrate. The comparison holds subsidy and average fees in BTC per block fixed. Actual payouts and operating costs vary.

Friday's adjustment reverses much of the relief miners received on Nov. 14, when mining difficulty fell 9.1%, and comes as deteriorating mining economics are already forcing operators to switch off machines.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

Blockchain analytics firm Glassnode reported that Bitcoin's network hashrate had fallen 8% year over year, marking its first annual contraction since China's 2021 mining ban.

While regulatory intervention forced miners offline in 2021, Glassnode attributed the current contraction to falling Bitcoin prices and record-low hashprice, a measure of the revenue miners generate per unit of computing power.

Data from Luxor's Hashrate Index showed that hashprice fell to $29.36 per petahash per day on Nov. 23, even as Bitcoin's seven-day average hashrate recovered 7.8% to 1,033 exahashes per second.

That short-term recovery in computing power helped drive Friday's difficulty increase, further compressing revenue for operators already contending with historically weak mining economics.

With Bitcoin's block subsidy fixed at 3.125 BTC, higher transaction fees could help miners offset the decline in revenue.

However, Mempool.space data showed that transaction fees averaged just 0.0265 BTC per block across the 128 blocks mined in the 24 hours preceding Friday's adjustment, accounting for less than 1% of mining rewards.

At an unchanged Bitcoin price, average transaction fees would need to increase roughly tenfold to 0.2664 BTC per block to offset the difficulty increase.

An unusually long block interval on Nov. 26 illustrates the scale of that challenge.

Alex Thorn, Galaxy Digital's head of research, noted that Bitcoin went 98 minutes and 19 seconds without producing a block, its longest interval since July and its 69th longest since 2011.

When Foundry USA eventually mined block 977,698, it processed 3,723 transactions and collected 0.1562 BTC in transaction fees.

Despite being nearly six times the average recorded before Friday's difficulty adjustment, those fees fell approximately 41% short of what miners would now need to earn consistently per block to restore their previous revenue at an unchanged Bitcoin price.

With transaction fees contributing so little to mining revenue, operators remain heavily dependent on a Bitcoin price recovery. A prolonged period of depressed prices could accelerate machine shutdowns, extending the network's annual hashrate contraction ahead of its next difficulty adjustment.

#5083. Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets

Home » Exchanges » Binance Rethinks VIP Eligibility as Investors Spread Capital Across Traditional and Crypto Markets

Binance expands VIP eligibility to include trading activity and asset holdings across external financial platforms.

Binance is adapting its VIP program to recognize financial activity across multiple markets, introducing a new initiative that allows investors to qualify for higher exchange status based on assets held and trading volumes generated on other platforms.

As cryptocurrency and traditional financial markets become increasingly interconnected, high-value investors are managing capital across a growing number of exchanges, investment products, and asset classes. Binance’s new VIP Status Match program aims to account for this shift by allowing individuals and institutions to demonstrate their financial activity beyond the exchange itself.

The initiative is part of a broader series of changes Binance has made to its VIP offering in 2026. In March, the exchange lowered BNB holding and Futures volume thresholds for VIP 1–3, introduced a Holder Program recognizing BNB and Alpha asset holdings across tiers up to VIP 9, and launched VIP Rising Star.

In July, Binance further reduced the wallet asset requirement for VIP 3 from $3 million to $1 million and began counting OTC Spot Volume at four times its value toward Spot Volume requirements.

The exchange also introduced a limited-time promotion running through the end of 2026, under which Stocks and bStocks trading volume counts at three times its value toward the 30-day VIP Spot Volume threshold. The initiative requires no registration and gives regular users and VIP 1–2 members a faster route to the next tier.

The latest addition, VIP Status Match, takes this approach further by allowing applicants to submit evidence of their 30-day trading volume or asset holdings on other digital asset exchanges or traditional financial platforms. Binance evaluates the information against its own VIP criteria to determine the appropriate tier.

Catherine Chen, Head of VIP & Institutional at Binance, said, “In 2024, we started recognizing trading activity from beyond crypto and we continue to refine our VIP Program to better reflect how our users engage across the platform. High-value users today trade and hold across multiple venues, so recognition should travel with them, not stay behind. Status Match does that, while keeping tier recognition tied to clear, measurable criteria.”

Both new and existing Binance users can apply. Applications are reviewed within three business days, and successful applicants receive an upgrade one tier above their qualifying level for 60 days, up to VIP 9. Upgraded trading fee rates take effect immediately upon approval, and participants are assigned a dedicated account manager.

Depending on their qualifying tier, users can also access benefits including VIP Earn, which offers up to 20% higher APR, Capital Connect for VIP 3 and above, customized API limits, sub-account management, and VIP events.

The program builds on Binance’s 2024 VIP Invitation Program but introduces broader eligibility. While the earlier initiative recognized trading activity beyond crypto, Status Match also accepts asset holdings as a qualifying metric and extends participation to existing Binance users.

The additional VIP tier is temporary. After 60 days, Binance will reassess participants against its standard requirements, including BNB balance, spot and derivatives trading volume, wallet assets, and 30-day average net borrowing. Users who meet the thresholds for their upgraded tier will retain it, while others will move to the level supported by their activity.

Through these changes, Binance is seeking to align VIP recognition with how investors allocate and manage capital across the wider financial ecosystem.

#5082. Bitcoin wallet privacy at risk? Researcher claims $0.35 attack could expose users’ IP addresses

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

This vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning users can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

To understand the vulnerability, it is important to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many users operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

According to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node announces the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

On the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Hence, as a potential workaround, users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the issue, but they remain unreleased.

Here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets currently at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.

#5081. The Best Yoga Pants for Women in 2026, Tested by Editors

Our style team basically lives in yoga pants. They've carried us from morning workouts, late-night deadlines, and weekend errands. Whether you prefer a pair of leggings with pockets or compression leggings, this is the *perfect* opportunity to pick out a new selection (or three!) for the season.

Curious about what makes a noteworthy pair of yoga pants? When deciding which types are the best, we went straight to the most trustworthy source: our Women’s Health editors. This list includes the best yoga pants our staffers say pass our rigorous sweat and wear tests.

After collectively testing more than 50 different yoga pants in the past three years, our team still gives top marks to Athleta's Elation Leggings for their buttery soft feel, flattering look, and supportive fit.

These wide-leg yoga pants are super affordable, but they don’t cut corners on quality or comfort. With a stretchy blend of spandex and polyester, these pants are super lightweight and made to move with you. The moisture-wicking material (which rivals that of some pricier yoga pants) pulls sweat from the body, keeping you comfortable throughout all your favorite yoga flows and workout classes.

#5080. BNB Chain Unveils New Ethereum-Compatible L1 Framework, Rules Out Separate Token

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. BNB Chain has outlined the architecture for a new Ethereum-compatible Layer 1 (L1) network, confirming that the proposed framework will not introduce a separate native token.

In an H2 2026 Tech Roadmap published in July 2026, BNB Chain stated that a next-generation L1 architecture was in development on a design path toward the 1 million TPS end-of-life goal and toward supporting different use cases than the existing ones. The plan was to ship it on testnet by the end of 2026, with mainnet release following in early 2027.

Fast forward to the close of November 2026, BNB Chain has introduced the Litepaper for the New L1, which describes the architecture being developed for high-frequency trading, payments, private finance and autonomous AI agents.

The design combines early transaction feedback, reserved capacity, native account controls and shielded settlement.

The new L1 is being developed alongside BNB Smart Chain, which remains the ecosystem’s broad-based network and streams small groups of transactions called SubBlocks before sealing a full block, with its public testnet being worked towards.

On the new L1, lanes reserve a share of block capacity for eligible activity, such as payments, while unused capacity returns to general traffic. This reduces competition from unrelated activity without guaranteeing that every transaction lands immediately.

The new L1 retains an Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)-compatible execution environment. Parallel EVM execution is planned, and protected ordering through a trusted execution environment (TEE) gateway has also been proposed.

BNB Chain invites the crypto community to participate in discussions on its Layer 1,  submitting their questions, use cases, and feedback to the BNB Forum.
