Such volatility can occur during the early trading period of a newly launched cryptocurrency, as buyers and sellers establish a market price. The token’s current distance from its latest high is therefore worth monitoring alongside its longer-term performance.

The November 26 CoinMarketCap snapshot showed a market capitalisation of approximately $3.01 million and 24-hour trading volume of about $155,650. It also reported approximately 2,180 holders. These figures provide a more recent view of market participation than the November 12 snapshot.

The token’s performance occurred during a difficult month for the broader crypto market. ConConAI says $CON’s movement has been driven by its own fundamentals, including a live product, transparent token information, and continued development. That explanation reflects the project’s position; price movement alone cannot establish what caused buying interest, and the broader market can still affect $CON.

Several developments give $CON a potentially constructive outlook as it moves beyond its initial listing period.

First, the token has established market visibility through its CoinMarketCap and CoinGecko listings, its reported first-day top-gainer position, and its early trading performance. Continued visibility could bring additional market participants to the project, although listings and past gains do not guarantee future demand.

Second, ConConAI has reported that 40.15 million tokens have been burned from the original 100 million supply, leaving an effective supply of 59.85 million $CON. The first two burns removed 20 million tokens each, followed by a monthly burn of 150,000 $CON on November 19. The project says further 150,000-token burns are scheduled monthly, with the next one planned for December 15. Future burns remain scheduled events until completed and verified on-chain.

Third, the token has a planned utility within ConConAI’s commercial network. If the platform attracts consumers and businesses, the intended use of $CON for partner listings, placements, and performance-based fees could create a more substantial demand story than trading interest alone. The development tracker currently places the first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

From the November 26 reference price of approximately $0.06582, a return to the November 24 high of $0.08434 would represent potential appreciation of around 28.1%. The combination of early market strength, reduced token supply, and an evolving utility model gives market participants several reasons to consider buying $CON.

ConConAI’s broader proposition is built around bringing back the personal purchase advisor, powered by artificial intelligence. Instead of navigating endless search results and comparing countless products, users describe what they need. A specialist AI advisor asks relevant questions, interprets the requirements, and returns one recommendation with the reason behind it.

The consumer remains in control. The AI does not make purchases on the user’s behalf, and the final decision always belongs to the user.

Seven specialist advisors are live, covering categories that include investment guidance, travel, cars, film, health information, music, and real estate. The project’s aim is to make AI useful in everyday purchasing decisions by helping people move from describing a need to identifying a relevant option.

Businesses can also submit products and services to the network. ConConAI’s stated model is that payment does not buy recommendation rank: a listing is intended to appear only when it honestly matches what the user asked for, with fit taking priority. This approach is designed to connect consumers with suitable offers while giving participating businesses another way to reach potential customers.

ConConAI says development capacity has been scaled up, with the listings system, advisors, and $CON payments now being built in parallel. Its public development tracker is updated as progress happens and identifies current work on partner listings, advisor improvements, and payment functionality. The project plans to begin its first partner payments in $CON in February 2027.

The exchange roadmap has also changed. ConConAI now says four Tier 2 centralized exchange listings are planned for December 2026, one after another. The project says each listing will be announced once confirmed. These are plans, not confirmed listing agreements, and should not be treated as guaranteed dates or outcomes.

The MEXC listing is currently on hold because of the exchange’s regulatory situation. ConConAI says it will review the situation from December 10, after which the MEXC listing may proceed or be replaced by another Tier 1 exchange. Until an exchange makes its own announcement or an agreement is confirmed, the plans remain subject to change.

The $CON presale sold out on November 4, and the token has traded on Uniswap v4’s official CON/ETH pool since November 6, 2026. Its liquidity position is reported to be locked with UNCX until November 6, 2028. The project says pool fees currently help cover development and marketing costs, with partner payments expected to contribute once the listings platform opens.

ConConAI reports that the live $CON contract audit has been completed. It also cites a TokenSniffer score of 100/100, contract verification on Etherscan, and listings on CoinMarketCap, CoinGecko, DEXTools, and DexScreener. These are useful verification and discovery signals, but they do not eliminate market, smart-contract or third-party platform risks.

The project’s transparency page provides live wallet balances and burn records. Its published allocation includes 30 million $CON for the community, 15 million for liquidity, 10 million for centralized-exchange liquidity, and approximately 5 million for project purposes. The project says its allocation wallets use Safe multisig arrangements. The official contract address is 0x7ad1A8Fc42Ac150B04dED5825D21a0C90b6d28D8.

$CON’s early market performance has given ConConAI a strong starting point following its Uniswap debut. Its ability to maintain interest will increasingly depend on trading participation, liquidity, product delivery, and the development of real commercial activity around its AI advisors.

If the project converts its existing development progress into wider consumer adoption and partner participation, the token’s intended utility could become an increasingly important part of its market proposition. Combined with the reported supply reduction and community-led roadmap, these factors provide a positive basis for watching $CON’s next phase, while recognising the volatility and risks associated with newly launched crypto assets.

ConConAI is developing a network of AI-powered personal purchase advisors and commercial partner listings. Its $CON token is intended to support partner activity across the ecosystem, including listings, placements, and performance-based fees.

#5078. Bit Digital borrowed against Ethereum to fund AI, and now its crypto treasury is paying the price

A $50 million Ethereum sale has halved the company's Galaxy debt, but substantial collateral exposure remains.

Bit Digital sold $50 million in Ethereum to repay a loan that helped finance its AI infrastructure expansion, but its remaining debt leaves the company's crypto treasury exposed to further financial pressure.

The Ethereum treasury company disclosed on Nov. 25 that it sold 29,825 ETH between Nov. 15 and 23 at an average price of $1,676, using the proceeds to halve its outstanding debt to Galaxy Digital to $50 million.

The sale marks a reversal of Bit Digital's original financing strategy. The company borrowed against its Ethereum holdings to help fund the expansion of its AI infrastructure subsidiary, WhiteFiber, while retaining exposure to ETH.

However, Bit Digital does not expect WhiteFiber to fully repay its bridge loan until the second quarter of 2027, while its agreement with Galaxy allows the lender to demand additional collateral within 24 hours.

Bit Digital borrowed against staked ETH to fund its AI infrastructure subsidiary.

The WhiteFiber bridge remained outstanding after Bit Digital paid down its Galaxy loan.

The filings leave draw-specific recall terms and collateral thresholds undisclosed.

The arrows show the direction of the original lending. The bars share a $100 million principal scale and compare Bit Digital’s reported Galaxy balances immediately before and after the November repayment.

The filings leave draw-specific recall terms and collateral thresholds undisclosed.

Kairos Research found that the value of the Ethereum collateral backing Bit Digital's $100 million Galaxy loan had fallen to about 131% of the outstanding principal as the company began moving ETH for sale.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

The research firm tracked approximately 24,800 ETH moving through Galaxy's hot wallet into Coinbase deposit addresses before Bit Digital publicly confirmed the sale, which ultimately accounted for around 18% of its Ethereum treasury.

During the period in which Galaxy delivered the ETH to Coinbase, Bit Digital's shares fell 15%, compared with a 4% decline in Ethereum.

Following the repayment, Bit Digital reported holdings of approximately 134,532 ETH and ETH equivalents, including 69,089 LsETH pledged against its remaining Galaxy debt and 36,811 ETH staked directly on Ethereum.

The pledged LsETH represents a substantial portion of the company's remaining treasury, leaving its financial position sensitive to further declines in Ethereum's price.

Under the master loan agreement, Galaxy can demand additional collateral when the value of pledged assets falls below an agreed threshold.

Bit Digital ordinarily has 24 hours from the issuance of that notice to provide additional collateral, although individual loan terms can impose shorter deadlines.

The company's quarterly filing also disclosed that its outstanding Galaxy borrowing at the end of September was callable on seven days' notice. The repayment announcement did not specify whether that provision applies to the remaining $50 million.

These obligations leave Bit Digital potentially needing to raise capital well before WhiteFiber returns the money it borrowed.

WhiteFiber's ability to repay its parent company could depend partly on its progress securing funding for the NC-1 data center.

On Nov. 9, WhiteFiber subsidiaries entered into a $300 million project financing agreement with a lender group represented by Morgan Stanley Senior Funding.

The agreement provides an initial $200 million facility, with funding conditions including operational readiness and customer acceptance of the data center's first 40 megawatts of capacity. WhiteFiber reported that no loans had been funded as of Nov. 10.

Access to the remaining $100 million requires further operational and financial milestones, including delivering financial statements covering the first three full calendar months after delivery.

The financing timetable leaves Bit Digital managing its Ethereum-backed debt while WhiteFiber works to unlock capital tied to progress on its infrastructure development.

#5077. Ripple’s XRP Ledger Lending Protocol Eyes Final Activation

The XRP Ledger lending protocol proposed by leading blockchain firm Ripple is making the headlines as it appears to be rapidly moving closer to its final debut.

The latest reports on its progress show that the protocol is just one validator vote away from concluding its mandatory approval process on the network.

Barely a few weeks after Ripple proposed a lending protocol on the XRP Ledger, the lending protocol amendment has already secured 28 of the 35 validator votes required to begin the approval process.

This marks major progress for the development, as the XRPL amendment system requires that a proposal earn more than 80% support from trusted validators for two consecutive weeks before it becomes permanently enabled.

While the approval period is mandated to restart if support falls below that level during the countdown, it appears that the Ripple lending protocol is already set to wrap up this process, as it is just one more vote away from reaching the 29-vote milestone.

This means that the lending vaults may be on track for their activation on December 9 if the lending protocol amendment retains the ongoing support.

With the proposed protocol drawing closer to its final launch, the XRP community has continued to express excitement as the proposal aims to introduce fixed-term, fixed-rate lending directly on the XRP Ledger.

As such, users will be able to deposit assets including the Ripple stablecoin and earn interest from borrowers, providing additional ways to earn money.

It is important to note that the proposal aims to provide exclusive opportunities for both lenders and borrowers while further expanding Ripple’s $837 million stablecoin market.

#5076. Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers

Home » Altcoins » Solana (SOL) » Solana Playground Adds AI Agent for Smart Contract Developers

The updated browser workspace adds an in-editor assistant as Solana expands its wider AI developer push.

Solana has rolled out a built-in AI coding agent inside Solana Playground, its browser-based development environment, aiming to help programmers learn, build, and deploy smart contracts without setting up local toolchains.

For traders and investors, it offers useful context on developer onboarding, Solana’s AI infrastructure push, and early-stage protocol risk.

In a post on X, Solana introduced the updated Solana Playground as a place to “learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser,” noting that the integrated agent explains existing code and edits it alongside the developer rather than writing full programs on its own.

Introducing Solana Playground – where you learn, build and deploy Solana programs right in your browser. An AI agent explains the code and edits it with you. Start here: https://t.co/nM0ySqDkfO pic.twitter.com/SFKYYTx04n

Builders can start projects using either Anchor, a framework that streamlines Solana program development, or native Solana programming, which offers lower-level control without framework abstractions.

According to product walk-throughs, the workspace includes three guided learning paths. These include an introductory Anchor tutorial called Hello Anchor and an intermediate build named Lumberjack. It also offers 10 sample Solana programs.

Browser-based Solana development predates the AI integration: the open-source Solana Playground (SolPg) has long let developers compile Rust programs, manage development wallets, and deploy contracts without a local CLI setup.

The latest release adds an in-editor assistant to explain unfamiliar code and apply edits within the same session.

The Playground update fits into a wider push around AI and automated agents on Solana.

Solana’s developer portal now provides guidance for AI coding agents, while solana.ai focuses on autonomous trading, wallet management, and stablecoin payments.

The Solana Foundation has also introduced an open-source Confidential Compute toolkit with Nito for AI workloads involving sensitive data.

Figures shared by the Solana Foundation at Breakpoint 2026 indicated more than 120 teams are building AI products on Solana, with access to the Builder Program for grants, technical resources, hiring support, marketing help, and infrastructure credits.

Developer-focused releases rarely drive sustained moves in SOL or ecosystem tokens on their own. Liquidity, macro conditions, and net capital flows carry far more weight in the near term.

However, lowering the barrier to write and iterate on code can speed up experimentation—and increase the volume of new or lightly tested contracts. Developer activity remains a key indicator of long-term ecosystem growth.

#5075. ‘Most bearish thing for XMR’ — What KuCoin’s Monero delisting means for liquidity

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

KuCoin is in the news today after announcing that it would remove Monero [XMR] spot trading on 30th November. The exchange’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs accounted for over half of Monero’s spot trading volume on CoinGecko.

With such a large trading venue leaving, where would Monero traders go next?

KuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC for 08:00 UTC on 30th November. Deposits have already been closed permanently too.

Withdrawals will close at 08:00 UTC on 31st December 2026. KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier over project-related issues, with the exchange also warning that stablecoin conversion of remaining balances won’t be guaranteed.

At press time, CoinGecko highlighted $90.42 million in combined 24-hour volumes across KuCoin’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs. Together, they accounted for 50.27% of Monero’s spot trading volume.

Including XMR/BTC and XMR/ETH, that brought KuCoin’s total to $104.60 million or 58.14%.

Hence, the question: Where could that trading move now? At the time of writing, the remaining exchanges showed more buy orders close to the market price, despite reporting a lower turnover.

Kraken’s XMR/USD pair had approximately $386,970 in buy orders within 2% below its price, compared to KuCoin’s XMR/USDT pair’s $85,683. WhiteBIT and HTX’s XMR/USDT pairs showed $260,810 and $196,231, respectively.

That gave Kraken roughly 4.5 times KuCoin’s nearby buying depth, with WhiteBIT and HTX also offering larger buy-side cushions. These orders could help absorb selling, although traders could cancel them at any time.

That access problem extended into services marketed as alternatives to CEXs.

X user and the founder of XMRHub called KuCoin’s delisting “the most bearish thing for $XMR.” According to the exec, the exchange supported swap services, liquidity, and onboarding.

Another X user, PerpetualCow, described the alleged connection more directly. He said,

Instant swap exchanges don’t have their own liquidity, they simply wrapped around Kucoin and sold/bought into their order books.

Still, the proposed dependency might explain why another exchange closure could affect apparently separate services. Swap interface routing orders through KuCoin would need another supplier, sufficient inventory, or a different execution route.

Dash’s Joel Valenzuela also raised a similar concern. He warned that further CEX losses could make no-KYC Monero swaps harder to obtain.

Finally, Cake Wallet founder Vik Sharma also directed users towards wallet-based swaps, writing,

Why does Monero keep getting delisted? Because it works!

The announcement followed another loss of exchange access earlier that month. MEXC ended XMR spot trading on 17th November. Its XMR Perpetual Futures closed separately on 13th November.

Kraken, for its part, had been explicit about its own rationale. It cited regulatory changes when halting XMR trading and deposits for European Economic Area customers on 31st October 2024.

#5074. To Heal Your Heart, Purge Your Playlist

Relationship experts explain why your choice of music can provide a fast-forward fix or replay the pain.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Since I was old enough to record playlists on cassette tapes, I’ve paired music with my intense crushes. Each guy basically had his own song, sometimes an entire soundtrack.

I fell in love with my college boyfriend to the tune of Bruce Springsteen’s “Dancing in the Dark,” while Miles Davis’s Kind of Blue was the anthem that played throughout a 15-year situationship with an elusive artist. Then, there was the whirlwind romance with a former smoke jumper turned ER doctor whose last concert was Emmylou Harris, which reminded me of the then-popular song “Emmylou” by First Aid Kit.

Each time, I became as obsessed with the song as the guy associated with it. My brain hyperfixated on the lyrics, first looking for hopeful clues, and then after the romance ended, sparking memories of sweet moments.

Music is often seen as a source of comfort for those dealing with heartbreak, but it can actually “arouse feelings of romantic longing, particularly searing melody,” says Walter Frisch, PhD, a professor of music at Columbia University. Some composers call such a haunting melody “l’idée fixe” or “fixed idea.”

Once that “fixed idea” gets stuck in your head—in the form of a song played on repeat—it can actually trigger the thoughts that land you in limerence, the involuntarily obsessive rumination on an idealized love interest. It’s fueled by both the hope that the person you like likes you back and the uncertainty of whether they do.

For a long time, I thought I was alone in my lyric-fueled limerence, but as I interviewed experts and other limerents as research for my memoir, When Longing Becomes Your Lover, I learned that it’s incredibly common—and normal—for our brains to connect music with unrequited lovers.

Neuroscience would call this melody intermittent reinforcement. When we are infatuated with someone, we are anticipating connection with that person, which results in our brain’s reward system releasing the “feel good” hormone dopamine. As a result, we are motivated to return to the behavior of deeply thinking, or ruminating, about them to get that reward.

In one famous MRI brain scan study, when heartbroken individuals were shown pictures of their heartbreakers, their dopamine pathways lit up just as they would from doing cocaine. Similarly, music can trigger someone to ruminate about what could be or what could have been with a romantic interest, says psychiatrist Jud Brewer, MD, PhD, the director of research and innovation at Brown University’s Mindfulness Center and author of The Craving Mind. The result, he says, is an itchy, contracted, restless feeling—quite the opposite of the expansive feeling associated with the mindfulness used to stop craving and anxiety.

Nostalgia also triggers the release of dopamine, and a song is like a time machine. Anytime I hear “Dancing in the Dark,” I’m instantly transported to kissing my college boyfriend in a dark, musty stairwell off campus. I can feel his hands resting on my hips and taste the Kentucky bourbon on his lips.

“There’s this certain charge you can get remembering somebody that you've been with before,” says Geoff MacDonald, PhD, a social psychologist who studies singlehood and sexuality at the University of Toronto. “You can replay, sort of viscerally, what it felt like to have somebody who was into you [and] that has the potential to provide real validation.”

He points to one study on song lyrics and attachment styles that, he says, “provides some evidence that people are drawn to a self-reinforcing bubble when it comes to intimacy.” In other words, it’s a form of confirmation bias. You’re drawn to songs with lyrics that reinforce what you already think about relationships, and you’re more likely to read into those lyrics and apply them to your own life.

For example, if you have an anxious attachment style—which many limerents do—you typically feel insecure in relationships and fear abandonment. Consequently, you may need constant validation, which is exactly what a certain song can provide. When I heard “Emmylou” playing on the radio one morning after the sexy smoke jumper had grown more distant over text, I decided it was a sign from the universe that we were still meant to be together. (It wasn’t.)

So, what’s a forlorn lover to do? Purge your playlist. “When someone is addicted to a behavior, if they avoid the people, places, and things [associated with the behavior], they’re less likely to get triggered to do the behavior,” says Brewer. “It’s not a great long-term solution, but it's one step that they can take.”

Think of songs that trigger you to ruminate, whether you’re obsessing over a crush or languishing over a lost love. Maybe it’s a song whose lyrics remind you of them, or a tune you danced to together. Whatever it is, consider removing that song from your playlist—at least until hearing the first few notes no longer launches you into a two-hour daydream about your love interest.

Now, if you've got a playlist that you play once every couple of weeks when you're feeling lonely, that can probably stay in your Spotify rotation. “It's good to remember that you can be loved,” MacDonald says. “But if you're leaning into that as a replacement for actually seeking real intimacy in your life, that's where you're going to run into problems.”

Instead of relying on songs to dream about relationships that would never materialize, I deliberately poured that relentless energy into hobbies that gave my life purpose. That might look like spending quality time with a loved one, creating art, or planning a trip—anything that takes your mind off the individual and fills your self-worth bucket.

Now, I can listen to Kind of Blue and “Emmylou” without yearning for past lovers, but I prefer playing songs that reinforce the security I feel in my marriage, like “Ain’t No Mountain High Enough,” the song we walked down the aisle to.

Amanda McCracken is a journalist, writing professor at the University of Colorado, the author of When Longing Becomes Your Lover, and the host of The Longing Lab podcast.

#5072. Japan weighs safeguards for Bitcoin holders who keep their own keys

One option in a regulator’s paper would make customers with new exchange accounts wait before sending crypto to their own wallets.

Japan’s Financial Services Agency returned to the issue of Bitcoin self-custody in a Nov. 26 paper for its study group. Japanese exchanges already have to record details of covered withdrawals. The paper asks what can protect customers once they hold the signing keys themselves.

An exchange manages the signing keys while it holds Bitcoin for a customer. In a self-custody wallet, the customer controls the keys needed to authorize a transfer. The FSA’s November discussion paper points out what happens if customers lose access to those keys. They may be unable to move their Bitcoin.

The Travel Rule requires providers to share information on certain transfers between them. An exchange sending Bitcoin to a customer’s own wallet has no receiving provider to notify. On a covered withdrawal, Japan’s recordkeeping rules require the exchange to collect and record details such as the destination wallet owner’s name and wallet address.

On a covered transfer from a self-custody wallet into the exchange without that notice, the exchange records the information it can obtain. The FSA’s supervisory guidelines cite the rules implementing Japan’s Act on Prevention of Transfer of Criminal Proceeds and call for exchanges to examine the wallet’s characteristics and assess its money-laundering risk.

The duties apply to exchanges that handle transfers. When two people transfer Bitcoin directly between wallets they control, neither has an exchange carrying out those checks. Under Switzerland’s planned crypto tax reporting, providers would report transactions they handle, while later transfers between personal wallets would fall outside that reporting.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

Two Bitcoin transfer routes show where a Japanese exchange has to keep a record and where users control the signing keys.

An exchange records details on covered withdrawals. In self-custody, the wallet owner controls the keys.

The exchange example covers outbound transfers without a Travel Rule notice.

The routes illustrate the providers and participants described in the FSA’s transfer explainer and supervisory guidance.

The exchange example covers outbound transfers without a Travel Rule notice.

The November staff paper cites a withdrawal waiting period for new exchange accounts as an example of an anti-fraud measure for a Cabinet Office ordinance. It gives no duration. Japan’s Diet passed amendments to the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and the Payment Services Act on July 15. As of Nov. 27, the FSA’s public rulemaking register listed no implementing ordinance or effective date for the proposed delay.

A February summary of the working group’s recommendations gave an example of how an exchange could intervene before a withdrawal. Immediately after opening an account, a customer could face a waiting period before sending crypto to a wallet they control.

In August, the FSA and Japan’s National Police Agency separately asked the industry’s self-regulatory association to strengthen withdrawal restrictions after cash deposits, crypto purchases or registration of a withdrawal destination. The request also called for scam warnings and transaction monitoring. The agencies also asked exchanges to check customers who make large or frequent withdrawals soon after restrictions lift.

For people who already hold their own keys, the November paper asks how to warn them about wallet risks and where regulation might help if problems arise. It also asks whether further measures are needed to curb money laundering and terrorist financing.

#5070. Midnight Savings Launch Puts NIGHT Ahead Of ADA

Home » Trendsetter News » Midnight Savings Launch Puts NIGHT Ahead Of ADA

Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout links banking activity more directly to NIGHT than ADA, but its £250M bid reflects initial capacity.

The £250 million figure attached to Monument Bank’s Midnight rollout is an initial capacity limit, not confirmed customer deposits, according to a video from crypto commentator FireHustle.

That distinction sits at the heart of the host’s analysis: a bank adopting technology built by Cardano’s developers does not necessarily translate into immediate demand for ADA.

Its potential significance lies less in the headline amount than in which token benefits from the activity.

According to Fire Hustle, Monument’s offering pays existing customers a fixed 5.2% for one year. Account details remain private, and customers cannot sell or transfer the blockchain records, even to another Monument customer.

Cardano’s Founder Charles Hoskinson celebrated the rollout with the phrase “250 million pounds on-chain.” But the host says Monument has not disclosed actual deposits, despite tokens representing the full initial allocation already having been created.

The YouTube video also cites Midnight Foundation president Fahmi Syed saying seven other banks are considering similar products: six in Canada and one in Japan.

Canada merits attention because Calgary-based digital-asset custodian Balance handles Monument’s tokens, according to the video. The host explicitly cautions against assuming the unnamed institutions are Canada’s six largest banks.

Midnight’s token structure is the investment question. The video says holding NIGHT generates DUST, the resource used to pay network transaction fees. Banks or service providers can therefore cover customers’ activity without requiring savers to handle tokens themselves.

“Somebody still has to hold the Night that makes the Dust,” she says. That creates a more direct connection between Midnight usage and NIGHT than between that usage and ADA, although additional activity does not guarantee token-price gains.

The ADA connection is more distant. Cardano stake-pool operators are expected to help secure Midnight in early 2027, with potential rewards extending to their ADA delegators. Those rewards are prospective, not existing income.

Fire Hustle reports ADA trading more than 90% below its peak at recording. However, the more useful indicators are actual Monument deposits, transaction volumes and confirmed bank launches.

#5068. The Right Kettlebell Can Upgrade Your Entire Strength Routine. These 5 Are the Best

We just changed our best adjustable kettlebell pick.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

WHEN YOUR HOME gym is short on square footage like mine, you need to carefully think about every piece of equipment before it earns its rightful spot. That’s exactly why kettlebells are a staple in my setup. Over time, I’ve built a small but mighty collection—and every single one gets regular use.

A huge perk of kettlebells is that they don’t hog a lot of space (even in a compact home gym) and are relatively inexpensive, says Tyneka Pack, CPT. These are versatile strength-training tools, too, allowing you to get in a full-body workout, along with explosive power movements, says kettlebell specialist Taylor Beebe, CPT.

As with any fitness equipment, improper use of kettlebells can lead to injury. That’s why most trainers, including Beebe, recommend getting coaching on how to use kettlebells before diving in (peep our how to get started with kettlebell exercises guide).

Like dumbbells, kettlebells come in a wide range of weights, materials, and grips, so it’s important to determine which type you’re in the market for before you buy.

After testing a handful of kettlebells, this cast-iron option from Amazon Basics earns its spot at the top of our list because of its budget price tag and versatile weight options. The weight range from 10 to 60 pounds has allowed me to ramp up my training intensity over time.

This kettlebell has consistently been my go-to and favorite even as I’ve expanded my collection. They’re surprisingly sturdy and durable, even after two years of use. WH fitness and reviews editor Natascha Grief also loves this model and has multiple in her home gym, too.

I own it in several weight sizes, and it has a compact shape that’s great for every kettlebell exercise imaginable. The grip is slightly textured and wide enough to do one- or two-handed exercises, but petite enough for smaller hands like mine. I can confidently hold it, even during potential wall-breaking moves like swings, and it’s comfortable to hold, whether I’m doing one set or five.

While these weights have a lot going for them, there is one con: There is no vinyl coating on the bottom (although there is a vinyl version, which WH editors also love). To avoid scratching my floors, I have to set it down carefully or use a mat underneath.

Many people prefer a competition-style kettlebell due to its uniform design that’s ideal for high reps and technical moves. The Rep Fitness Adjustable Kettlebell offers a competition-style kettlebell shape with adjustable weights, giving you plenty of space-saving mileage out of one tool.

This kettlebell is well-designed, stacking five weights in one relatively compact design. (Weight ranges include 8 to 16 kilograms, 16 to 24 kilograms, and 20 to 40 pounds.) To adjust the weight, just push down on the dial with two fingers, twist to your desired weight, and lift. It has a rubber base to protect your floors although—heads up—the rubber coating is only there when you use the kettlebell’s full weight. Otherwise, you’ll want to set down your kettlebell gingerly.

REP’s adjustable kettlebell is made from cast iron and feels durable. The textured handle is easy to grip and has plenty of space for two-handed moves, although it feels slightly wider than others. If space is a premium at your place and you’re looking to grow with your kettlebell, this is a solid choice.

Read More: Best Compact Home Gym Equipment

If you prefer a more traditional competition-style kettlebell, keep scrolling. But if you’re on the hunt for a highly versatile weight that aims to combine the attributes of a kettlebell with those of a dumbbell and a dual-grip medicine ball, the YBell Neo Series is worth consideration.

This weight is perfect for my needs—it’s relatively compact and offers multiple ways to grip, thanks to its unique pyramid-style design. I can use it for everything from biceps curls to lunges, though it’s not ideal for swings.

The grip on this is perfection. It features a neoprene outer layer to create a slightly sticky feel with impressive gripping power, so I’m not stressed about accidentally flinging it across the room during swings. The wide handle leaves enough room for one- or two-handed exercises, but it may feel a little crowded using both mitts at once if your hands are on the larger side.

You have three different spots you can grip on the outside of this weight, along with an inside bar that’s ideal for dumbbell-style work. While the sides are rounded, I found it was relatively easy to rest the YBell on its base or sides to save space.

The only potential downside of this weight is that it tops out at 26 pounds. If you’re interested in doing heavier lifting, you’ll need to upgrade to a different device.

A coated kettlebell like this one from Yes4All protects your floors in case of butterfingers through a thoughtfully wrapped coating up the bottom third of the handle. The handle itself makes for a comfortable grip. Fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi says, “I have the 15-pound model and I never feel it slipping away from me when squatting or doing Russian twists.” It comes in five-pound increments up to 65 pounds, giving you plenty of options.

While I wouldn’t recommend tossing this on your floor at home, the kettlebell doesn’t make a loud noise when it’s dropped, unlike uncoated models. It’s also worth pointing out it’s very affordable, similar to our best overall.Just note the bottom of the kettlebell is not entirely flat, which can be tricky if you’re trying exercises like uneven pushups (with one hand placed through the handles of a KB).

Sand kettlebells are a highly portable option that allows you to add a little more instability to your kettlebell workouts. The GoRuck Sand Kettlebell is built tough thanks to its Cordura nylon design and multiple closure system, so you don’t have to stress about accidentally spilling its contents all over the place.

GoRuck’s kettlebell has a teardrop-style shape that works well for many exercises. This kettlebell arrives empty, so you’ll fill it up with sand prior to use. Pro tip: use playground sand available at home improvement stores for this. The reinforcing on nearly all of the seams and bottoms means you can toss this on the ground without worrying about it flying open and spilling sand everywhere.

This style of kettlebell isn’t for everyone, but if you’re looking to add the extra challenge of sandbag training to your kettlebell workouts, this sand kettlebell design will take a lot of abuse and holds up well over time.

“When choosing the correct weight for your kettlebell, it is important to consider your exercise,” says Almoni Ellis, CSCS, CPT. She says that people generally are able to use heavier weights when doing purely lower-body exercises, but that those weights may be too heavy for a person when they’re doing a move like an overhead press, for example.

That said, there’s no one-size-fits-all starting point. Your experience level and current strength come into play, so if you’re unsure where to begin, try testing different weights at a local gym or consider ordering two sizes to see what feels best. As your strength improves, you can gradually increase the weight, adds Pack.

The most common option for general strength training is the cast-iron kettlebell, which works well for everything from goblet squats to cleans to swings. These are the kettlebells you’ll most often see in home gyms and fitness classes.

Ellis and Pack recommend choosing a cast iron or steel kettlebell because they’re the most durable and long-lasting materials. “Kettlebells [that are] made up of plastic[...] don’t last as long,” Pack says.

However, most adjustable kettlebells are made with some plastic components, which is necessary for the design. As for vinyl-coated kettlebells, they’re usually made of cast iron with a vinyl coating to prevent damage to floors.

Handle thickness plays a role in both comfort and performance. “Thicker handles can help build grip strength, but they may be more challenging for beginners to control,” says Pack.

The handle’s coating and texture matter just as much. A slightly textured surface can help you maintain a secure grip, especially during dynamic or high-rep movements. Slick handles, on the other hand, can become slippery as your hands sweat—raising the risk of losing your grip, Pack adds. If you’re training with kettlebell that has a slick grip, consider using workout chalk or liquid chalk during moves like swings.

To choose the best kettlebells, I consulted three personal trainers who regularly work with kettlebells: Taylor Beebe, CPT, Tyneka Pack, CPT, and Almoni Ellis, CSCS. I also got feedback from Women’s Health fitness and reviews editor Natascha Grief, NASM-CPT, who is a certified trainer.

Based on their feedback, I focused on crucial features to look for in these super versatile strength-training tools. I then tested some of the most popular kettlebells out there. Each was put through a slew of workouts to test its efficiency, durability, weight, material, and grip. Because every person’s budget is different, I made sure to include kettlebells with a range of price points.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Could the next 24 hours confirm Bitcoin’s bottom?

Bitcoin is down over 20% in November, marking its steepest monthly correction since June. Back then, BTC recovered from $55K to $85K over the next three months. A similar recovery now depends on reclaiming key resistance levels and flipping the market structure bullish. For starters though, BTC needs to establish a bottom.

At the time of writing, Glassnode data revealed that BTC was still defending its summer lows. August’s breakout above $80K has since fully retraced, bringing price back to June’s $60K support zone.

Although BTC briefly wicked below this level twice, every daily candle has closed above it. This could be a sign that buyers are defending this support level.

Meanwhile, other on-chain metrics are lending weight to the bottoming thesis.

Bitcoin’s stablecoins have lost $21 billion in the last two months, mirroring what happened in 2022. Back then, a $33 billion reduction in stablecoin supply occurred ahead of BTC’s November low, suggesting that the current liquidity contraction could signal a similar market reset. On the flip-side though, reduced stablecoin liquidity reduces the funds that can be used to stimulate a market rally.

This puts the focus on the next 24 hours. Around $6.8 billion in Bitcoin Options are set to expire on Deribit at 08:00 UTC. With the put/call open interest ratio at 0.89 and heavy put positioning around $60K, the expiry could fuel further market volatility and test Bitcoin’s [BTC] bottoming structure.

Bitcoin’s latest Options expiry could prove critical.

On-chain data revealed that nearly $6.8 billion in Bitcoin Options will expire on Deribit, marking one of the month’s largest expiries. Max pain sat at around $70K-$73K, while BTC traded near $60.9K, leaving a gap of roughly 15%. Meanwhile, the put/call ratio climbed from 0.55 in October to 0.89. This suggested that traders have been becoming more defensive and adding protection against a potential Bitcoin price decline.

Interestingly, the main bearish zones seemed to be at $60K, $58K, $50K and $40K. Significantly, $40K put options expire on Christmas Day. Meanwhile, Bitcoin ETFs have continued to show net redemptions for seven days running. For the month of November alone, $5.39 billion has been redeemed, the highest ever monthly figure.

Consequently, the real test will now come after expiry.

Traders are placing more bets on Bitcoin’s price falling. At press time, put options were high at strike levels of $60K, $58K, $50K and $40K. However, maximum pain was indicated to be at significantly higher levels, showing a wide gap between current prices and Options positioning. Generally then, with the growing put/call ratio and elevated short interest, it would seem that traders may be bracing for further downside. They might not be anticipating a swift rebound either.

In short, Bitcoin is showing early signs of a potential bottom. However, shrinking stablecoin liquidity, record ETF outflows, and rising demand for downside protection allude to the presence of bearish pressure. The $6.8 billion Options expiry could add volatility, putting the critical $60K support to the test.

#5066. Bitcoin’s turbulent week has created a $16 billion opportunity for a short squeeze

Bitunix sees resistance at $62,000. A Nov. 26 CryptoQuant snapshot estimated $16 billion in potential short liquidations across Bitcoin prices of $60,000 to $100,000.

Bitcoin is trying to recover after a volatile week. If buying carries it higher, leveraged short sellers forced to close their positions could add to the rebound.

Bitcoin traded at $61,436 at 13:09 UTC on Nov. 27, down 0.2% over the previous seven days, according to CryptoSlate’s Bitcoin price tracker.

Bitcoin climbed above $64,000 on Monday following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, which also drove the chipmaker's shares 31% higher and helped major US equity indices register their strongest sessions in more than a year.

However, the cryptocurrency surrendered its gains within hours and subsequently fell below $58,000 as concerns about the sustainability of the AI investment boom resurfaced.

Glassnode’s market analysis described Bitcoin’s reversal as an early sign that investors were selling into strength. The Nasdaq came under pressure a day later. However, global markets showed renewed signs of recovery on Friday. S&P 500 futures rose nearly 2%, Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 2.8%, and Dow Jones futures gained 655 points ahead of a shortened US trading session following Thanksgiving.

Equities across Asia and Europe also advanced, providing a more favorable backdrop for Bitcoin as bearish bets against the digital asset accumulate.

CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost noted that Bitcoin's price struggles this week have pushed its short-term holder market value-to-realized value (MVRV) ratio to 0.85, approaching the 0.81 reading recorded during the market's July 1 downturn.

The indicator measures the relationship between the market value of Bitcoin held by short-term investors and their aggregate acquisition cost, providing insight into the financial pressure facing recent buyers.

The ratio peaked at 1.18 on Sept. 22, when short-term holders were sitting on average unrealized profits of approximately 18%.

The subsequent decline has erased those gains, leaving the cohort with average unrealized losses of around 15% and an estimated cost basis of $71,600.

Darkfost said similar periods of financial stress have coincided with past Bitcoin bottoms, when prices traded below recent buyers’ acquisition costs.

Alphractal CEO Joao Wedson identified similar patterns across previous Bitcoin halving cycles, noting that the broader MVRV ratio's historical trajectories have remained remarkably consistent despite differences in the magnitude of price fluctuations.

According to Wedson, the current cycle's valuation trajectory suggests Bitcoin may be approaching the final stages of one of its strongest accumulation opportunities.

“History may not repeat itself perfectly, but the cyclical behavior of Bitcoin remains difficult to ignore.”

At the UTC afternoon price, Bitcoin would need to rise about 16.5% to reach that estimated cost basis.

Meanwhile, the derivatives market has developed a substantial liquidation imbalance that could accelerate such a recovery if buying demand returns.

CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju’s Nov. 26 Bitcoin liquidation map estimated $16 billion in potential short liquidations across prices from $60,000 to $100,000, against less than $5 billion in potential long liquidations below that range.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

Reconstructed from approximate $500-step screenshot bars, with cumulative amounts rounded to $0.1 billion. Long exposure falls toward zero as BTC price rises to $60,000; short exposure accumulates above $60,000. The short-side plateau follows the source screenshot, not verified future outcomes. Figures are model estimates; underlying CryptoQuant CSV was unavailable.

Source: CryptoQuant — BTC Estimated Liquidation Levels, screenshot supplied Nov. 27, 2026

A move through nearby resistance would still leave much of the $60,000 to $100,000 range untested.

“Short squeeze fuel is piling up for the next rally, imo.”

An upward price move could force leveraged traders betting against Bitcoin to close their positions, adding buying pressure and potentially accelerating the cryptocurrency's recovery.

CryptoSlate tracked a similar short-squeeze setup on Nov. 20, when a sell-off left a large cluster of shorts vulnerable to a price rebound. In the latest figures supplied by Bitunix, open interest rose while trading volume fell.

Analysts at crypto exchange Bitunix told CryptoSlate that Bitcoin's trading volume had declined nearly 47% over the preceding 24 hours, while liquidations fell approximately 69%.

Open interest, however, rose 1.2% to 1.5% over the same period, indicating that outstanding derivatives exposure grew despite the slowdown in trading activity.

Meanwhile, cumulative volume delta (CVD), which measures the difference between aggressive buying and selling, remained negative across both spot and futures markets.

Bitunix said Bitcoin's ability to rebound despite negative CVD suggests that buyers are absorbing selling pressure, although aggressive buying demand has yet to materialize.

The analysts identified $62,000 as Bitcoin's immediate resistance level, followed by a more concentrated supply zone between $62,400 and $62,640. Cardano is already looking beyond its upcoming Dijkstra hard fork, with Euler emerging as the next major upgrade.

In a recent release, Intersect, a member-based organization in the Cardano ecosystem, said it is planning the next Cardano upgrade, Euler, with the first meeting of the Euler Scoping Working Group scheduled for December 1, 2026, at 5 p.m. UTC. Here, participants will contribute to early discussions on the scope of the next Cardano era.

The development signals Cardano's continued commitment to evolving its blockchain infrastructure through a structured upgrade process. While Dijkstra represents the current focus, discussions on Euler will set the tone for what comes next for the network.

The Dijkstra era delivers Cardano's major protocol upgrade in two phases: Phase 1, Dijkstra hard fork (Protocol Version 12), introduces the Dijkstra ledger era and ships Ouroboros Linear Leios as a complete, activated feature. The second phase activates Ouroboros Peras via an intra-era hard fork. Peras is a settlement-speed upgrade that adds a voting overlay to the existing Ouroboros Praos chain selection rule.

As of the latest update by Intersect, Dijkstra ledger features are currently being tested on DijkstraNet, while Linear Leios consensus and throughput are being tested on MusashiNet. Both are converging toward Node 11.3, which is the target hard fork release candidate.

The Dijkstra upgrade requires both constitutional and technical changes in the era of on-chain governance. Discussions and refinements on constitutional guardrails (Update Constitution) or CAP-12 "Dijkstra era parameters" continue on the Constitutional Amendment Portal ahead of Mainnet submission.

Protocol Version 12 has already gone live on Musashi and DijkstraNet, while a hard fork release candidate (11.3) is required for Preview and Preprod hard forks. In its recent post, Intersect sets the Dijkstra hard fork target timeline as December 2026 for the Preview network, including the Update Constitution and hard fork.

On-chain activation of the Update Constitution action on the mainnet is expected in December 2026, while the Dijkstra hard fork is expected in Q1 2027.

#5064. Kristin Juszczyk on the Science and Style Behind Venus Williams’ F1 Look

The designer’s custom trench and corset called attention to how little sports science research focuses on women.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

The Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix is one of the most glamorous weekends in sports. With drivers’ global followings and a long list of A-listers in attendance, the event can feel as much like a fashion show as a race.

But while many guests were focused on the designer labels, Kristin Juszczyk had another message in mind: the need for more research on women in sports.

Juszczyk is a self-taught designer whose work began as a hobby and has since made her a force in the industry. The wife of San Francisco 49ers player Kyle Juszczyk, her custom game-day outfits gained traction on social media, and she has gone on to dress high-profile names including Simone Biles, Taylor Swift, and Caitlin Clark. This year, she was also named to TIME’s 100 Most Influential People in Sports.

For the Las Vegas GP, Juszczyk partnered with Gatorade’s Body of Science, an initiative dedicated to advancing the research on women’s sports. One stat drives their research: 6 percent of sports science research focuses on women.

Only 6 percent of published research in sports and exercise journals has focused exclusively on women, per a study published in the Women in Sport and Physical Activity Journal—a staggering gap that has implications for everything from training to recovery, as previously reported by Women’s Health.

Tennis legend Venus Williams, a Gatorade athlete, wore a custom look Juszczyk designed for the paddock red carpet inspired by this staggering statistic.

“Venus is one of the most iconic athletes of our generation, and to have her being in one of my designs, is surreal,” Juszczyk exclusively tells Women’s Health.

When it came to building the design, Juszczyk says she first took inspiration from motorsport fashion while also channeling the ambience a city like Las Vegas brings to the race. She opted to use leather as the base material, feeling like it channeled the energy of the sport. From there, she designed a trench coat with a layering corset piece over it, an homage to the city’s glitz and glamour.

Designing a trench coat was a first for Juszczyk, but the corset design is what she describes as her personal “bread and butter.” True to the Gatorade brand, the trench featured piping in its iconic orange, offset with black.

That 6 percent statistic is also front and center, ensuring the message of the design is clear: There needs to be more research dedicated toward women’s sports.

Juszczyk wanted to stay true to Venus and her personal style, and did a lot of research on what she wears on the regular. She says she approaches all of her designs with intentionality, ensuring the client is wearing something they feel good in.

“I want it to feel like my design, but I still want it to be something they feel beautiful and confident in,” she says.

The look was on full display when Venus presented the winner of the F1 Academy race, Alisha Palmowski, with her trophy. The moment was symbolic: a titan of women’s sports celebrating the new generation, while calling attention to a research gap that directly affects them.

“If anyone can take anything away from it, it’s that women need as much research in sports as men do,” she says. “The world is doing so much in pushing women athletes forward, and science should back it as well.”

Alyssa Cruz is the social media editor at Women’s Health, where she drives social strategy and helps shape the brand’s voice across platforms. Prior to WH, she worked at CBS News and palabra. Originally from Toledo, she is a proud alumna of Ohio University, where she received two bachelor’s degrees in journalism and Spanish. When she is not creating social content, you can find her trying different restaurants in New York City or planning her next trip.

#5063. Analyst: Ripple’s Growth Doesn’t Guarantee $10 XRP

Home » Trendsetter News » Analyst: Ripple’s Growth Doesn’t Guarantee $10 XRP

Ripple’s expansion alone won’t send XRP to $10, a popular wealth coach states.

A $10 XRP would imply a circulating market value of roughly $630 billion, not simply another rally on Ripple announcements.

That is the central argument from Dr. Kamilah Stevenson, a wealth coach whose latest YouTube video episode examines why the company’s institutional expansion has not translated into the token price many holders expected.

Using approximately 63 billion XRP in circulation, Stevenson argues that reaching that XRP valuation requires more than partnerships and regulatory milestones. It requires sustained demand to own the token, rather than merely move money through it.

Stevenson separates Ripple’s corporate performance, adoption of its products, demand for XRP and the token’s market price. Those categories overlap, but they are not interchangeable: a customer using Ripple’s custody services or stablecoin does not necessarily need XRP.

Even payments routed through XRP may generate limited lasting demand. In the process she describes, a payment provider buys the token, transfers it and sells it into the destination currency within seconds, allowing the same inventory to support repeated transactions.

“Big payment numbers alone don’t automatically push the price up,” Dr. Stevenson says. The more consequential question is how much XRP participants need to keep available between transactions.

Market makers may hold inventory to support larger payment flows, creating a potential link between usage and ownership. Still, the video does not quantify how much additional inventory those flows would require.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson cites roughly 1.19 billion XRP held by ETFs and about 473 million held by Evernorth, a company established to accumulate XRP. Those are figures presented in the video, rather than independently verified current totals.

Her distinction is useful: XRP-backed fund holdings represent direct token ownership, while the national trust bank approval she attributes to Ripple does not itself require institutions to purchase XRP.

Supply remains part of the calculation. Stevenson puts Ripple’s escrow holdings at around 31 billion XRP, with up to one billion released monthly and unused amounts returned to escrow. An unlock is therefore not equivalent to an immediate market sale.

The sharper test is whether an announcement creates incremental buying, how long those tokens stay held and whether new supply offsets that demand. Dr. Stevenson remains bullish, but the adoption figures she discusses do not establish when XRP reaches $10.

Ethereum developers have agreed to move ahead with the next step in the Glamsterdam upgrade.

The key takeaway? Reaching consensus was not easy. Developers flagged potential network disruptions and usability issues with the new gas opcode. Still, they decided to proceed with it. In fact, the team also agreed to schedule the Hoodi testnet upgrade for 15th December at 7:12 PM UTC, moving Glamsterdam testing closer to implementation. So, what does this tell us?

As highlighted in the developer’ discussion, Ethereum is emphasizing post-quantum security within its development, in addition to focusing on on-chain enhancements. Simply put, regardless of the ongoing concerns, the developers are clearly moving away from just looking at scaling and speed, and towards ensuring Ethereum is future-proof in relation to quantum computing.

The meeting focused on deciding the scope and timing of the Glamsterdam upgrade and the prioritization of post-quantum security features. The execution layer teams reached a rough consensus to proceed with the current Glamsterdam spec as is, with the Hoodi testnet upgrade scheduled for December 15 at 7:12 PM UTC.

Interestingly, this was also reflected in the debate around the upcoming Heze upgrade.

There was debate about whether to support Fossil or to place a bigger emphasis on post-quantum work. Concern was expressed that Fossil may also require development effort. Though no conclusion was reached, the matter will be discussed further at the next team meeting. Meanwhile, Kevaundray suggested that Keccak256 should be used as the hashing algorithm for Ethereum’s post-quantum work.

Against this backdrop, the Heze upgrade moving forward does not seem far-fetched. With the Hoodi upgrade scheduled and Keccak256 proposed for post-quantum security, Ethereum’s [ETH] focus on strengthening its long-term security is now becoming clearer.

The Hoodi testnet is a testing version of Ethereum that allows developers to trial upcoming upgrades.

Think of it as a testing ground where developers can identify bugs and ensure upgrades like Glamsterdam work smoothly before reaching Ethereum users. Within the wider scope of Ethereum’s post-quantum development, it may also be used to test new security features, again allowing developers to analyze how prepared they are to then apply these to the mainnet.

That makes Hoodi an important test for Glamsterdam, giving developers a clearer picture of whether the upgrade is ready for mainnet. Why does this matter? Well, Glamsterdam aims to improve transaction processing. If successful, these changes could strengthen Ethereum’s network fundamentals. Here, the timing matters too.

As the chart shows, Ethereum has processed just over 100 million transactions in Q4 so far. By comparison, the network averaged more than 200 million transactions per quarter in 2026. This puts Q4 activity well below its recent pace, with ETH’s technical structure also showing signs of weakness.

Against this backdrop, the Hoodi testnet upgrade could mark an important inflection point for Ethereum.

A successful rollout would bring Glamsterdam closer to mainnet deployment. In turn, the upgrade could boost Ethereum’s throughput, improve execution efficiency, and support stronger on-chain activity.

Ethereum developers are moving ahead with Glamsterdam while focusing more on future quantum security.

The Hoodi testnet will help test the upgrade before mainnet, with the goal of making Ethereum faster and more efficient.

#5060. Bank of England to test how UK finance would recover from an AI disruption

The voluntary 2027 exercise will examine whether financial firms can restore services together when several face disruption at once.

The Bank of England will use a frontier AI scenario in its 2027 operational stress test to see how a disruption involving advanced AI could affect UK finance. One question is whether firms’ recovery plans would work together if several institutions faced disruption at once. The voluntary, exploratory exercise will examine both individual firms and the wider sector.

The Bank set out the plan for its Cyber and Operational Resilience Stress Test in its Nov. 26 Financial Stability Report. It is discussing possible scenarios with firms, industry groups and technical experts. The Bank plans to invite suitable participants for testing in summer 2027 and publish findings on common themes in the fourth quarter.

The Bank’s Financial Policy Committee record warned that a weakness at a common supplier could disrupt several firms and financial market infrastructure at once. A firm can test how quickly it would restore its own operations. The committee said risks can remain across the system even when individual firms have credible fallbacks. A Solana routing outage showed how a shared provider can disrupt independently run infrastructure. Validators representing about 29% of stake stopped voting when one provider’s routing failed.

A problem at a shared provider can hit several firms at once. Their separate recovery plans have to work together to keep services running.

Credible fallbacks at individual firms can still leave gaps in the services the sector needs to restore.

The firms shown are hypothetical. The Bank is still discussing scenarios for the voluntary 2027 frontier AI exercise.

Illustrative network diagram based on the Bank’s discussion of shared providers and collective recovery. Arrows show how disruption and recovery dependencies can connect firms and services.

The firms shown are hypothetical. The Bank is still discussing scenarios for the voluntary 2027 frontier AI exercise.

In its wider resilience work, the Bank is examining whether firms’ workarounds can collectively sustain a minimum level of activity in retail and wholesale payments and sterling interest-rate markets. In those markets, a priority is keeping settlement of UK government bond trades running. That work illustrates the stakes of joint recovery while the Bank weighs scenarios for the AI exercise.

Please enable JavaScript to verify and send this form.

The Bank says a prolonged interruption to retail payments could leave households and businesses unable to make or receive essential payments. In wholesale payments, disruption could tie up cash and collateral and leave firms unsure when incoming payments will arrive, putting pressure on other obligations.

An October survey by the Bank and the Financial Conduct Authority shows where firms already rely on the same providers. The three largest cloud and computing providers accounted for 79% of reported relationships in that category. The three largest providers of model access and hosting accounted for 54% of reported relationships in theirs.

The survey also found that adoption of AI agents was widespread among respondents and broad autonomy was rare. Among firms that answered the respective questions in the full survey, 80% said they had deployed AI agents and 2% said they had deployed agents with broad autonomy.

The Bank’s stress-test program includes a separate 2026 exercise on disruption involving a cloud provider and third parties, with findings planned for summer 2027.

#5058. ASEAN+3 announces new initiative to discuss digital asset regulations — Details

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Given the rise in the acceptance of digital assets, the ASEAN+3 member countries have agreed to establish a dedicated working group to advance discussions on cross-border digital payments and regulatory approaches to digital assets.

The decision was announced in the Co-chairs’ Statement following the ASEAN+3 Finance and Central Bank Deputies’ Meeting held in Kyoto, Japan recently.

Here, the initiative aims to strengthen regional financial cooperation by improving payment connectivity and encouraging discussions on how crypto should be regulated across participating economies.

In fact, it also marks a step towards greater coordination among Asian financial authorities as digital assets and blockchain-based financial services continue to expand.

To make this successful, the proposed working group aims to operate under the newly established AMRO Cross-Border Digital Payments Program. Under the same, they will provide a dedicated platform for ASEAN+3 economies to discuss retail and wholesale payment connectivity, alongside regulatory approaches to digital assets.

This is particularly important because cross-border payments remain fragmented across different financial systems. Needless to say, differences in payment infrastructure, regulations, and compliance requirements make international transactions slower and more expensive.

However, with greater coordination, participating economies could explore inter-operable payment systems and more consistent regulatory approaches.

Interestingly, the development also comes amid broader efforts by governments and financial regulators to address the growing influence of cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, and tokenized assets.

One prominent example is the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework. It became fully applicable on 30th December 2024, following the introduction of stablecoin-specific provisions in June 2024.

For those unaware, MiCA establishes common rules for crypto-asset issuers and service providers, covering authorization, transparency, investor protection, and market conduct. Its implementation has provided a regulatory benchmark for other jurisdictions considering comprehensive crypto frameworks.

South Africa is another example of this shift. In August 2026, the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) and National Treasury proposed an activity-based reporting framework for cross-border crypto transactions.

The proposal focuses on identifying and monitoring transactions that could facilitate capital flight, illegal financial flows, or regulatory circumvention. Rather than classifying crypto assets as official currency, it seeks to bring their cross-border movement under closer financial safeguards.

On the other hand, the United States has faced setbacks in establishing similar regulatory clarity. The proposed Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act failed to advance in the Senate on 15th September, receiving 49 votes in favor and 50 against. it was short of the 60 votes required to proceed.

Its failure has left the U.S without the proposed comprehensive federal market structure framework, potentially putting it behind jurisdictions such as the E.U in providing regulatory certainty. However, the SEC and CFTC continue to pursue regulatory initiatives under their existing authority.

Against this backdrop, ASEAN+3’s latest decision is the latest in the world’s global regulatory discussion/efforts.

#5057. Strength-Train Your Hair

Can the slew of products designed to fortify weakened strands really made a difference? Dermatologists and beauty scientists detail what to look for when you’re shopping the haircare aisle

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

WE’D ALL LIKE to imagine our hair as strong, resilient, healthy. And there’s no shortage of products marketed toward reaching that end point. You’ve got your bond-building treatments, your protein masks, your strengthening serums—heck, there are now entire product lines geared toward promoting robust, rugged strands.

But what exactly does it mean to have ‘strong’ hair?

We tend to equate strength with the kind of glossy, thick, bouncy strands you'd see in a shampoo commercial. But there’s more to the science than that. For starters, hair that looks healthy isn't necessarily strong, and hair that's naturally fine or thinning isn't automatically weak. Plus, there's a difference between making hair “feel” stronger and actually improving its ability to withstand breakage.

Meet the experts: Sherry Maragh, MD, is a board-certified dermatologist based in Virginia. Nathan Puksta is the founder and CEO of FILAMENT Sciences, a haircare brand focused on the science of stronger hair.

So, what counts as strong hair, and can all these products really deliver on their promises? We asked two experts to explain.

Scientifically speaking, hair strength is all about resilience, meaning how well an individual strand withstands stress from brushing, stretching, styling, and other everyday activities without breaking. That strength largely comes from two parts of the hair shaft: the cuticle, which acts as its protective outer layer, and the cortex, which contains keratin proteins responsible for much of its structural integrity, explains Sherry Maragh, MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in Virginia.

Another important factor is elasticity, or the ability of hair to stretch and return toward its original shape without snapping. One of the most useful measurements is tensile strength, which quantifies how much force a strand can withstand before breaking, says Nathan Puksta, the founder and CEO of FILAMENT Sciences, which creates products and ingredients dedicated to the science of stronger hair. Think of it as the difference between a brittle piece of dry spaghetti and a flexible rubber band.

Tensile strength is an important part of this conversation because it’s something that laboratories can actually measure, using calibrated equipment that pulls individual hair fibers until they break. Other tests evaluate elasticity, breakage, and resistance to combing. But strength isn't synonymous with thickness, density, or shine. "Hair can absolutely be strong while still being fine, thin, or less reflective," says Dr. Maragh. "Similarly, hair that appears thick and glossy is not necessarily resistant to breakage." In other words, those naturally fine strands might be remarkably resilient, while locks that epitomize the “glass hair” trend could be surprisingly fragile.

Unfortunately, the things we regularly do to make our hair look good can also compromise its strength. Puksta identifies five major contributors to weakened hair: chemical processing, mechanical damage, heat, environmental exposure, and aging.

Chemical treatments, particularly bleaching and certain straightening processes, can be especially damaging because they alter the hair's internal structure. But everyday habits matter, too. Those can look like:

So, can you actually make your hair stronger? Yes, but there's an important distinction between improving damaged hair's performance and returning it to its original, undamaged condition. "The visible hair shaft is made up of nonliving cells, so damaged hair cannot biologically heal in the way skin does," says Dr. Maragh.

That doesn't mean strengthening products are useless. Certain ingredients can improve hair's physical properties, reduce friction, reinforce weakened areas, and help prevent additional breakage, with some technologies even working beneath the cuticle. Puksta explains that bond-building treatments target chemical interactions within hair, while certain peptides and proteins can help reinforce its keratin structure. However, effectiveness varies considerably between formulations.

Dr. Maragh cautions that an ingredient's ability to penetrate the hair shaft doesn't automatically prove that it repairs structural damage. So, what can different strengthening products realistically accomplish?

And remember that a product claiming 80 percent stronger hair isn't necessarily saying what you think. Dr. Maragh recommends examining what was measured, the comparison group, and whether results came from laboratory testing or consumer feedback. Protein retention, for example, isn't the same measurement as tensile strength.

A 2026 Women’s Beauty Award winner, this wash is prized for its ability to deeply hydrate and help detangle, cutting down on pulling while brushing. It also contains ingredients that battle oxidative stress on the scalp, helping follicles hang onto hair for longer.

A solid conditioner that helps detangle and cut down on styling damage is worth its weight in gold. Dove’s product contains a peptide complex that helps to repair damage.

Oribe Hair Alchemy Fortifying Treatment Serum

This serum contains a curative complex of chia seed, plant protein, and bio-fermented bamboo leaf that the brand claims can penetrate the cortex to heal from within. But perhaps its biggest plus is that it can protect hair from heat damage up to 450 degrees.

FILAMENT TS.02/Tt: Tensile Strength Hair Treatment Mask

Featuring a patented complex that improves hairs’ tensile strength, this mask also contains a plant oil blend for moisturization and protection.

In a small study conducted by the brand, this biotin-free bioactive blend was shown to support hair density and thickness.

Here's the good news: You don't need naturally thick, glossy hair to have strong hair. And if your strands are damaged, there are meaningful ways to improve their resilience. The key is understanding what products can—and cannot—accomplish. A conditioner that reduces breakage through easier detangling is valuable, even if it doesn't rebuild internal bonds. Likewise, a treatment that improves measurable tensile strength isn't necessarily reversing every aspect of previous damage (translation: it can’t recreate virgin hair).

Ultimately, maintaining strength is as much about preventing damage as treating it. Consistent conditioning, gentler styling practices, and choosing products suited to your hair type can help protect existing strands while healthy new hair grows.

And that's worth remembering the next time you see a bottle that promises stronger hair: The goal is helping the strands withstand whatever you put them through—not just have shampoo commercial-worthy hair.
